main.name: Main stories
main.subtitle: The game's three long stories: the main quest, Dragonborn and Dawnguard
main.more: Each runs for many hours. In LoreRim, Miraak's cultists come at level 25 once you've finished The Way of the Voice, and Dawnguard waits for level 30.

guilds.name: Guilds and factions
guilds.subtitle: Join a guild or a side and work your way up
guilds.more: The Companions, the College, the Thieves Guild, the Dark Brotherhood, the Bards College and the Civil War, plus orders that mods add, like the Vigilants of Stendarr.

daedric.name: Daedric Princes
daedric.subtitle: Quests for the Daedric Princes, most ending in an artifact
daedric.more: LoreRim holds almost all of them back until level 20, and Hircine until 25. Lines that mods add, like Saints and Seducers, are here too.

lands.name: New lands
lands.subtitle: Quests that take you to places outside Skyrim
lands.more: Solstheim, Wyrmstooth, Hammerfell, Morrowind's border, realms of the dead and more. Most are made for level 20 and up.

side.name: Side stories
side.subtitle: Shorter quests in towns, ruins and on the road
side.more: The longest list: the base game's side quests and the ones mods add. Most take an hour or two.

followers.name: Followers
followers.subtitle: Quests that come from your followers
followers.more: Bring them along and their quests come to you. Serana's also belongs to Dawnguard.

work.name: Jobs and errands
work.subtitle: Notice boards, bounties and favours for townsfolk
work.more: Missives boards in every hold, bounties from the jarls, and odd jobs for the people of each town. They come back, so pick one up whenever you like.

lines.name: The main quest
lines.begins: I have been captured by the Empire and sentenced to death alongside the Stormcloak rebels. We were taken to Helgen, but before I could be executed a dragon appeared and attacked the town. I need to find some way to escape.
lines.start: Take a Dragonborn start: Helgen Keep (Start) or Helgen Keep (End).
lines.gate: None. After Before the Storm, Balgruuf no longer walks you to Farengar: the Dragonstone task waits until you ask Farengar about the dragons.

unsure.why: The Resting Pilgrim note may be part of the Dragonborn start (Matlara's inn behaviour runs while this quest is already under way) or a separate way in from other starts; Alternate Perspective's start quests and Matlara's dialogue aren't in these files.
The start menu offers "Helgen Keep (Start)" and "Helgen Keep (End)"; the records don't spell out how much of the escape the End option skips.

Alternate Perspective changes the journal text so the Empire captured Ulfric (not you), which suggests you aren't one of the prisoners; the records hold both versions and don't settle which one shows.
The quest script also holds Fury, Conjure Spirit Wolf and Sparks spells; nothing shows the player is given them in normal play, so they're left out.
Helgen doors (Resting Pilgrim, houses, Skalei's Scrap) are tied to an Alternate Perspective switch that hides them; when exactly it flips isn't in these files.

The weapons and prisoner clothes are properties on the vanilla quest script; with Alternate Perspective you aren't a prisoner, so AP's gold, Stitched Boots and Clothes may replace them. Which set the player actually gets isn't shown.

quests.name: Bleak Falls Barrow
journal: Jarl Balgruuf thinks I may be able to help Farengar, his court wizard, with something related to dragons.

Farengar Secret-Fire, Jarl Balgruuf's court wizard, has asked me to retrieve a Dragonstone from Bleak Falls Barrow, a stone tablet that he believes contains a map of ancient dragon burial sites. He hopes this will help him understand how and why dragons are returning to Tamriel.

Farengar Secret-Fire, Jarl Balgruuf's court wizard, asked me to retrieve a Dragonstone from Bleak Falls Barrow, a stone tablet that he believes contains a map of ancient dragon burial sites. quests.name: The Way of the Voice
journal: The Greybeards have summoned me to their monastery of High Hrothgar on the slopes of the Throat of the World. They seem to have learned of the mysterious power that I gained when I killed the dragon outside Whiterun.

The Greybeards summoned me to their monastery of High Hrothgar on the slopes of the Throat of the World. I spoke to Arngeir, one of the Greybeards, who believes that I am "Dragonborn", which means I am especially gifted in the use of the Voice. They have offered to help me learn to use my new abilities.

The Greybeards summoned me to their monastery of High Hrothgar on the slopes of the Throat of the World. Their leader, Arngeir, recognized me as "Dragonborn", and taught me more about my new Voice powers. After passing several tests, they sent me on one final trial, retrieving the legendary Horn of Jurgen Windcaller.

quests.name: A Blade in the Dark
journal: Delphine, the innkeeper in Riverwood, is more than she seems. She was the one that left me the note in Ustengrav. She gave me back the Horn of Jurgen Windcaller. She went to a lot of trouble to get my attention. I should find out what she wants.

Delphine believes that dragons are coming back to life and that the next one will resurrect near the town of Kynesgrove. Once I've convinced her that I'm Dragonborn by killing the dragon, she promises to fully explain who she is and what she wants with me.

Delphine believes that dragons are coming back to life and that only the Dragonborn can stop them. Near Kynesgrove, we saw a dragon Shouting another one back to life. That dragon is dead, and now it's time for Delphine to give me some answers.

Delphine believes that dragons are coming back to life and that only the Dragonborn can stop them. It turns out that she was right. Near Kynesgrove, we saw a dragon Shouting another one back to life. After we killed the dragon and I absorbed its power, Delphine accepted that I was Dragonborn as she had hoped, and revealed that she is one of the last members of the Blades, an organization dedicated to protecting the Dragonborn and stopping the dragons.

journal: It seems that things are worse than even Delphine thought. Dragons aren't just coming back to life, they're being resurrected by other dragons. Delphine suspects that the Thalmor might be bringing dragons back for some sinister purpose. She's going to talk to her contacts about how we can infiltrate the Thalmor Embassy.

She's going to help me infiltrate the Thalmor ambassador's manor and find out what they know about the dragons. I should meet with her contact, Malborn, in the Winking Skeever Inn in Solitude.

journal: I've gotten to the Blades loremaster Esbern ahead of the Thalmor. I hope he's as knowledgeable about dragons as Delphine promised.

I found the Blades loremaster Esbern and brought him to Riverwood to talk to Delphine. quests.name: The Throat of the World
journal: With Esbern's help, I've deciphered Alduin's Wall in Sky Haven Temple. It revealed that Alduin was defeated in ancient times by a Shout of some kind. Maybe the Greybeards can teach me this Shout, or at least tell me how I can learn it.

With Esbern's help, I've deciphered Alduin's Wall in Sky Haven Temple. It revealed that Alduin was defeated in ancient times by a Shout of some kind. Arngeir knew the name of the Shout, "Dragonrend", but could not teach it to me. However, he has agreed to show me the way to reach Paarthurnax, the Greybeards' leader, who lives at the top of the Throat of the World. Arngeir says that Paarthurnax is the only one who may know this Dragonrend Shout.

With Esbern's help, I've deciphered Alduin's Wall in Sky Haven Temple. It revealed that Alduin was defeated in ancient times by a Shout of some kind. Arngeir sent me to talk to Paarthurnax, who he said was the only one who might know this Dragonrend Shout. It turns out that Paarthurnax is actually a dragon.

Arngeir sent me to talk to Paarthurnax, the Greybeards' leader, who turned out to be a dragon. Paarthurnax didn't know the Dragonrend Shout, but believes that there's a way for me to learn it from the ancient heroes who used it against Alduin.

quests.name: Alduin's Bane
journal: I've located the Elder Scroll that was used to cast Alduin forward into our time by the Nord heroes of old. If Paarthurnax is right, if I read it near the Time-Wound I will get a vision of the past, when the ancient Nords used the Dragonrend Shout against Alduin.

I read the Elder Scroll near the Time-Wound, and learned the Dragonrend Shout in a vision of the Nord heroes fighting Alduin in the distant past. Now I need to use Dragonrend to defeat Alduin in the present time.

I read the Elder Scroll near the Time-Wound, and learned the Dragonrend Shout in a vision of the Nord heroes fighting Alduin in the distant past. When I returned from the vision, Alduin attacked me, and I used Dragonrend to bring him down and defeat him.

quests.name: The Fallen
journal: After I defeated Alduin on the top of the Throat of the World, he fled from me. I need to locate his lair so I can finish him off, once and for all.

After I defeated Alduin on the top of the Throat of the World, he fled from me. One of his dragon allies may be able to tell me where he's gone. I've learned that Dragonsreach, the jarl's palace in Whiterun, was once used to imprison a dragon. I need to persuade the Jarl of Whiterun to help me trap a dragon in Dragonsreach.

After I defeated Alduin on the top of the Throat of the World, he fled from me. One of his dragon allies may be able to tell me where he's gone. I've learned that Dragonsreach, the jarl's palace in Whiterun, was once used to imprison a dragon. If I can arrange a truce in the civil war, the Jarl of Whiterun has agreed to help me trap a dragon in Dragonsreach. Then I can interrogate the dragon and learn the location of Alduin's lair so I can finish him off, once and for all.

After I defeated Alduin on the top of the Throat of the World, he fled from me. One of his dragon allies may be able to tell me where he's gone. The Jarl of Whiterun has agreed to help me trap a dragon in Dragonsreach. Now I need some way to lure a dragon into the trap. Esbern or Paarthurnax might be able to help.

After I defeated Alduin on the top of the Throat of the World, he fled from me. One of his dragon allies may be able to tell me where he's gone. After I defeated Alduin on the top of the Throat of the World, he fled from me. One of his dragon allies may be able to tell me where he's gone. The Jarl of Whiterun has agreed to help me trap a dragon in Dragonsreach. I've learned a Shout which is the name of one of Alduin's allies, which should serve to bring him to the Dragonsreach courtyard so I can trap him there. Then I can interrogate the dragon and learn the location of Alduin's lair so I can finish him off, once and for all.

After I defeated Alduin on the top of the Throat of the World, he fled from me. One of his dragon allies may be able to tell me where he's gone. With the help of the Jarl of Whiterun, I've trapped the dragon Odahviing in Dragonsreach. Now to interrogate Odahviing and learn the location of Alduin's lair so I can finish him off, once and for all.

After I defeated Alduin on the top of the Throat of the World, he fled from me. One of his dragon allies may be able to tell me where he's gone. journal: I've passed through Alduin's portal into Sovngarde, the realm of Aetherius where the souls of Nord heroes go to feast and battle until the final reckoning. Now to find Alduin and defeat him once and for all.

I've passed through Alduin's portal into Sovngarde, the realm of Aetherius where the souls of Nord heroes go to feast and battle until the final reckoning. Alduin has laid some kind of soul-snare across the valley of Sovngarde, a mist where he hides and feeds upon the trapped souls. My only hope is to reach the Hall of Heroes.

I've passed through Alduin's portal into Sovngarde, the realm of Aetherius where the souls of Nord heroes go to feast and battle until the final reckoning. Alduin has laid some kind of soul-snare across the valley of Sovngarde, a mist where he hides and feeds upon the trapped souls. I reached the Hall of Heroes and met Gormlaith Golden-Hilt, Hakon One-Eye, and Felldir the Old - the three heroes who I saw defeat Alduin in my vision of the past. They have been permitted by Shor, the god of the underworld, to join me in my battle against Alduin.

read.about: Dragons have come back to Skyrim, and this is the story of the Dragonborn sent to stop Alduin, starting with a dragon attack on Helgen and running through Whiterun, High Hrothgar, the Blades and beyond. It has 19 story quests plus four side jobs for the Greybeards and the Blades.

getIn.where: Helgen, in Falkreath hold
getIn.how: Pick the Dragonborn start ("You are the Dragonborn of legend, saving the world from Alduin.") at Helgen Keep, either at its start or its end, and escape the dragon attack.

order.what: Escape Helgen through the keep during a dragon attack, with Hadvar or Ralof.
Go to Riverwood, then tell Jarl Balgruuf in Dragonsreach about the dragon.
Fetch the Dragonstone from Bleak Falls Barrow for Farengar, the Jarl's court wizard.
Go with Irileth to the Western Watchtower, where a dragon is attacking, then report back to the Jarl.
Climb from Ivarstead to High Hrothgar and train with the Greybeards.
Retrieve the Horn of Jurgen Windcaller from Ustengrav for Arngeir.
Meet Delphine in the attic room of the Sleeping Giant Inn, then go to Kynesgrove and kill the dragon Sahloknir.
order.where: Sleeping Giant Inn, Riverwood, and Kynesgrove

order.what: Get into the Thalmor Embassy, either at the ambassador's party with Delphine's help or by storming it, and search it.
Find Esbern, a Blade hiding in the Ratway under Riften.
Take Esbern to Delphine in Riverwood, then find Sky Haven Temple past the Forsworn camp at Karthspire.
Learn Clear Skies from the Greybeards and climb to Paarthurnax at the summit.
Find the Elder Scroll, by way of the College of Winterhold, Septimus Signus, Alftand and Blackreach, at the Tower of Mzark.
Read the Elder Scroll at the Time-Wound on the summit.
Find a way to trap a dragon in Dragonsreach and question it.
Arrange a truce in the civil war at a council at High Hrothgar, so the Jarl of Whiterun will help.
order.needs: Only while the civil war is still being fought

order.what: Free Odahviing and let him fly you to Skuldafn.
Cross the mist of Sovngarde to the Hall of Valor.
Help the heroes in the Hall of Valor drive off the mist and face Alduin.
Decide Paarthurnax's fate after Delphine and Esbern demand his death.
A radiant job that can come up when you enter High Hrothgar: find a Word of Power in a dungeon the game picks. It isn't a step in the story.

gives: Thane of Whiterun, with Lydia as your housecarl (Dragon Rising)
Blade of Whiterun, a greatsword, and enchanted armour from Requiem's reward list (Dragon Rising)

Shouts: words of Unrelenting Force and Whirlwind Sprint (The Way of the Voice), a word from Wulfgar (The Horn of Jurgen Windcaller), Clear Skies and a word of Fire Breath (The Throat of the World), Dragonrend (Alduin's Bane) and Call Dragon (The Fallen)
The power of the dragons you kill at the Western Watchtower and at Kynesgrove (Dragon Rising, A Blade in the Dark)

unsure.why: No minimum level or level gate for this line is in the records (no GetLevel condition on its opening), so the level it is made for isn't given.

A note in the Resting Pilgrim in Helgen says talking to Matlara about staying longer may start something; whether that is a way in from other starts or part of the Dragonborn start isn't in the records. How the line begins after other character starts isn't shown either.
Paarthurnax: no record shows which earlier quest must be done before Delphine and Esbern turn on him.

Rebuilding the Blades and Dragon Research: nothing in the records shows what starts them; they likely follow Alduin's Wall, when Delphine and Esbern move into Sky Haven Temple. Paarthurnax Quest Expansion edits them, so the Paarthurnax choice may lock or delay them.
Season Unending: if the civil war is already over, the truce step may be skipped; the script that decides this isn't in the records.
The Jarl's armour rewards in Before the Storm and Dragon Rising are Requiem leveled lists; which piece you get isn't shown.
If you spare Paarthurnax, whether the Blades refuse to help you for good or only until you talk them round isn't in the records.

Season Unending's truce talks name holds on each side and two towns (Karthwasten and Darkwater Crossing) that can be traded; if any change hands that could cost a side or a place, but the terms and what happens to them aren't in the records.
Elder Scroll (Dragon) is the reward of Elder Knowledge, but the records don't say whether you keep it after reading it in Alduin's Bane.

quests.name: Prophet
journal: When I returned to Fort Dawnguard, Isran told me that he needed to speak to me, and he asked me to follow him.
When I returned to Fort Dawnguard, I was surprised to learn that Serana had come to the base searching for me. She claimed to have something urgent she needed to tell me.
When I returned to Fort Dawnguard, I was surprised to learn that Serana had come to the base searching for me. She claimed to have something urgent she needed to tell me.

Serana told me that her father was trying to gain power over the sun by fulfilling a prophecy found in the Elder Scrolls. If we could read the prophecy, we might be able to stop him. Serana had one of the scrolls, but we'd need a moth priest in order to read it.

Serana told me that her father was trying to gain power over the sun by fulfilling a prophecy found in the Elder Scrolls. If we could read the prophecy, we might be able to stop him. Serana had one of the scrolls, but we'd need a moth priest in order to read it.

Serana told me that her father was trying to gain power over the sun by fulfilling a prophecy found in the Elder Scrolls. Only a moth priest can read an Elder Scroll, so we've set out to find one.

Eager to unlock the secrets of an ancient prophecy thought to be hidden within Serana's Elder Scroll, Harkon has ordered his court to find a moth priest. I now have reason to suspect that there's a moth priest in Solitude.
Serana and I heard a rumor that a moth priest recently visited Solitude. He was thought to have stayed at the Winking Skeever.

Serana told me that her father was trying to gain power over the sun by fulfilling a prophecy found in the Elder Scrolls. We've set out to find a moth priest who can read Serana's Elder Scroll, and the trail has led us to Dragon Bridge.
Serana and I are one step behind the moth priest. We journeyed to Dragon Bridge and learned that he had passed through the town, heading south across the bridge.

I'm one step behind the moth priest. After leaving Dragon Bridge, I searched along the road for any sign of his passing. I found an overturned wagon and some dead vampires and Imperial guards. Was this the moth priest's wagon?

I'm one step behind the moth priest. After leaving Dragon Bridge, I searched along the road for any sign of his passing. I found an overturned wagon and some dead Imperial guards and vampires. Was this the moth priest's wagon?
Harkon's vampire agents have captured the moth priest and taken him to a place called Forebears' Holdout. I must rescue him before the vampires can break his will.

Harkon's agents have captured the moth priest! I have tracked them to Forebears' Holdout, but the vampires have enthralled the moth priest and I will have to confront him in order to break their hold.

Harkon's agents have captured the moth priest! I have tracked them to Forebears' Holdout, but the vampires have enthralled the moth priest and I will have to confront him in order to break their hold.
Harkon's agents captured the moth priest and enthralled him, but I was able to break their hold on his mind.
I rescued the moth priest from his vampire captors and asked him to meet me at Fort Dawnguard. I must return to Isran and tell him of our success.
With the moth priest safely back at Fort Dawnguard, he can now read Serana's Elder Scroll and learn more about the prophecy that Harkon is hoping to use to gain power over the sun.
With the moth priest safely back at Fort Dawnguard, he can now read Serana's Elder Scroll and learn more about the prophecy that Harkon is hoping to use to gain power over the sun.

After the moth priest's reading, we have more questions than answers. The old priest saw a vision of a weapon called Auriel's Bow, but we need to find two more Elder Scrolls in order to unravel the rest of the prophecy.

quests.name: Chasing Echoes
journal: Dexion's reading of the Elder Scroll has given rise to more questions than answers. The moth priest saw a vision of a weapon called Auriel's Bow, but Serana and I need to locate two more Elder Scrolls in order to unravel the rest of the prophecy.

Serana has indicated her desire to locate her estranged mother, Valerica, who had fled Castle Volkihar with one of the Elder Scrolls. She believes that Valerica may have left a clue to her whereabouts somewhere in the courtyard of the castle. In order to avoid detection by Harkon, we've decided to utilize a hidden entrance on the back side of the island.

Serana has indicated her desire to locate her estranged mother, Valerica, who had fled Castle Volkihar with one of the Elder Scrolls. She believes that Valerica may have left a clue to her whereabouts somewhere in the courtyard of the castle. In order to avoid detection by the castle's vampires, we've decided to utilize a hidden entrance on the back side of the island.

Serana and I are trying to locate her mother, Valerica, who may have one of the Elder Scrolls. Our journey has taken us to the courtyard of Castle Volkihar where we've discovered a hidden entrance underneath Valerica's old moondial.

Serana and I are trying to locate her mother, Valerica, who may have one of the Elder Scrolls. Our journey has taken us beyond the courtyard of Castle Volkihar where we've discovered a hidden entrance underneath Valerica's old moondial. After exploring the ruined tower beyond, we've stumbled across an old alchemy laboratory. Serana is convinced her mother has hidden some notes that may yield a clue as to her whereabouts.

Serana and I are trying to locate her mother, Valerica, who may have one of the Elder Scrolls. Our search has taken us to Valerica's laboratory hidden within the ruined tower at Castle Volkihar. According to Valerica's notes found there, she has likely fled Tamriel and entered the Soul Cairn, a dimensional plane of Oblivion. In order to pursue her into the Soul Cairn, Serana and I need to recreate the experiment that opens the portal to this strange place.

Serana and I are trying to locate her mother, Valerica who may have one of the Elder Scrolls. In Valercia's laboratory, we've recreated an experiment she performed and opened a portal to the Soul Cairn, a plane of Oblivion. Serana believes strongly that her mother is inside this strange place and has indicated we should step through.

When attempting to step through the portal to the Soul Cairn, a hidden force that seems to be draining my life energy is preventing me from entering. I have two choices if I wish to enter the Soul Cairn. I can allow Serana to change me into a vampire, thereby "killing" me in effect. Alternatively, I can allow her to partially soul trap me which could potentially weaken me while I roam the Soul Cairn.

Serana and I have stepped from Valerica's laboratory on Tamriel to a plane of Oblivion known as the "Soul Cairn" in order to find her mother Valerica. Serana strongly believes if we can find her, she will be able to tell us the location of one of the Elder Scrolls we need to decipher the Tyranny of the Sun prophecy.

quests.name: Beyond Death
journal: Serana and I have entered the Soul Cairn in pursuit of her estranged mother, Valerica, and the Elder Scroll she took when she fled Castle Volkihar.

Serana and I have located Valerica imprisoned within a massive ruin. When confronted by us, Valerica revealed that Serana's blood is an integral part of the Tyranny of the Sun. After the reconciliation between the two of them, Valerica confessed to having the Elder Scroll hidden in her ramshackle living space. In order to free her from the prison, Serana and I will have to locate and slay the Keepers who maintain the barrier around the ruins.
Serana and I have slain all three of the Keepers and the barrier around Valerica's prison has faded. We rejoined Valerica, who has agreed to take us to the location where the Elder Scroll is hidden.
As Valerica was leading us to the Elder Scroll, an ancient dragon named Durnehviir swooped into the ruins and attacked. It proved to be a challenging battle, but we've emerged unscathed.
We've exited the Soul Cairn with the Elder Scroll in hand. Serana's mother, Valerica, is unwilling to return with us to Tamriel until we've dealt with her husband and thwarted the Tyranny of the Sun.

quests.name: Unseen Visions
journal: After discovering that Dexion has become blind, I've had to secure alternate means to decipher the Elder Scrolls and locate Auriel's Bow. It's been suggested that I might be able to read the Elder Scrolls myself if I use an ancient technique performed by the original moth priests. I'm now on my way to a place known as the Ancestor Glade to discover the origin of the mysterious ritual.

I've used the unusual knife to collect the bark from the canticle trees dotting the Ancestor Glade, which has in turn drawn ancestor moths to me. I've felt a surge of energy run through my body and I feel drawn towards the large column of light in the center of the glade.

I'm now standing in a column of light which appears to stretch into the sky at the center of the Ancestor Glade. According to Dexion, I've completed the Ritual of the Ancestor Moth and can now read the Elder Scrolls. I'll need to begin with the Elder Scroll I obtained from the Soul Cairn in order to decipher the location of Auriel's Bow.

After entering the column of light in the Ancestor Glade, I was able to read the Elder Scrolls. I had an incredible vision that pinpointed a cave entrance far away on the western edge of Skyrim. This appears to be the location of Auriel's Bow. If I'm to stop Harkon from completing the Tyranny of the Sun, I should hasten there immediately.

quests.name: Touching the Sky
journal: The vision provided by the Elder Scrolls seems to indicate that Auriel's Bow may be located in a place known as Darkfall Cave. I should proceed there as soon as I'm prepared if I wish to recover the bow and stop Harkon from completing the Tyranny of the Sun.

The vision provided by the Elder Scrolls seems to indicate that Auriel's Bow may be located in a place known as Darkfall Cave. I should proceed there as soon as I'm prepared if I wish to recover the bow and stop Harkon from completing the Tyranny of the Sun.

I've encountered Gelebor, a snow elf Knight-Paladin of the Chantry of Auri-El. He's requesting I kill his brother, Arch-Curate Vyrthur, who's been corrupted by the Falmer. I've been given an Initiate's Ewer which will ultimately provide me access to the Chantry's Inner Sanctum where both Arch-Curate Vyrthur and Auriel's Bow are located.

I've completely filled the Initiate's Ewer given to me by Knight-Paladin Gelebor. All that remains is gaining access to the Chantry's Inner Sanctum where both Arch-Curate Vyrthur and Auriel's Bow are located.
I've gained access to the Chantry's Inner Sanctum. I should find and confront Arch-Curate Vyrthur in order to secure Auriel's Bow.

It's been revealed to me that the Tyranny of the Sun was created by Arch-Curate Vyrthur as his revenge upon Auriel for rebuking him when he was turned into a vampire. He possessed Auriel's Bow, but still needed the blood of a pure vampire to complete his ritual. This placed Serana in mortal danger, and I had no choice but to destroy him. I now possess the final piece of the Tyranny of the Sun, Auriel's Bow.

quests.name: Seeking Disclosure
journal: In order to locate Auriel's Bow, the moth priest, Dexion, indicated that two other Elder Scrolls would be required. The first scroll foretells the interactions of the dragons with the history of Nirn. The second foreshadows the defiance of the gods with the blood of mortals.

I've secured both of the Elder Scrolls needed to fully decipher the Tyranny of the Sun and pinpoint Auriel's Bow. I need to return to Fort Dawnguard where Dexion has been waiting to begin his reading.

I've secured both of the Elder Scrolls needed to fully decipher the Tyranny of the Sun and pinpoint Auriel's Bow. I need to return to Castle Volkihar where Dexion is imprisoned so he can begin his reading.

After bringing the Elder Scrolls to Dexion, a disturbing development has arisen. When reading the first scroll in front of Harkon's court, he wasn't able to fully prepare himself and he's become blind. It's now up to me to bring all three Elder Scrolls to the Ancestor Glade where I can supposedly unearth an ancient method of reading them myself.

read.about: Vampires are stirring in Skyrim, and this story has you choose between the Dawnguard vampire hunters at Fort Dawnguard, southeast of Riften, and the vampire court of Lord Harkon at Castle Volkihar. Each side has about a dozen story quests, with radiant jobs for the side you choose.

Lord Harkon dies (Kindred Judgment)

Stalf and Salonia Caelia die (The Bloodstone Chalice)
The three Boneyard Keepers die (Beyond Death)
Dexion Evicus is left blind and can't read the scrolls any more (Seeking Disclosure)
On Harkon's side: the Dawnguard leaders are targets in Destroying the Dawnguard (Isran, Sorine Jurard, Gunmar, Florentius Baenius, Agmaer, Durak, Celann and Beleval)
Your spouse becomes a vampire (The Gift); the person you bite becomes a vampire (New Allegiances)

unsure.why: No minimum level or level gate for this line is in the records (the opening has no dialogue or event conditions), so the level it is made for isn't given.
Who first tells you the Dawnguard are recruiting isn't in the records; the opening quest has no start line, event or script in these files.

The radiant jobs' offer conditions aren't in the records; which side each belongs to comes from the job system that starts it. For New Allegiances, Rings of Blood Magic, Amulets of Night Power and Destroying the Dawnguard, nothing limits them to Harkon's court, though they are handed out at Castle Volkihar.
Whether the radiant jobs repeat isn't shown; the quest records carry no repeat flag. Their payment is likely gold and a leveled list held by the job system, but which job pays what isn't recorded.

Both Prophet versions likely follow A New Order or The Bloodstone Chalice; their journals only say "when I returned", and the records don't show the link. Bolstering the Ranks overlaps A New Order's own Florentius step in a way the records don't show.
Power of the Blood: Skip Vampire Lord Tutorial edits it last, but the change isn't shown, so that it's skipped comes from that plugin's name.
Whether you can change sides after Bloodline isn't in the records. Whether a player who is already a vampire gets the Chasing Echoes choice isn't shown.

A Vampire Lord Ornament is held by Kindred Judgment's script, and the Dawnguard War Axe by Bloodline's; whether either is given to you, and on which side, isn't shown. Whether you keep the rings and amulets from the court's jobs isn't shown either.
In Destroying the Dawnguard, whether every one of the eight must die, or whether any are protected, isn't in the records.
Summon Arvak is held by the Soul Cairn Horse Quest's script; the records don't show which step gives it.

quests.name: The Temple of Miraak
journal: After freeing the Skaal from the magic controlling them, Storn, the shaman, has asked me to seek out a member of their tribe who is still missing. I need to look to the temple near the center of Solstheim to find Frea and make sure she is safe.
I've found Miraak's temple on Solstheim. Now I need to find out why people are trying to kill me on his behalf.
I was successful in defeating Miraak after he attacked me, but he has disappeared. I should search his temple to learn more about what's going on here.
I've found Frea, a warrior from the Skaal Village on Solstheim. She is also searching the Temple of Miraak, looking for answers. We've agreed that we need to find where Miraak's power is coming from.

After delving through the Temple of Miraak, Frea and I have discovered a strange book deep within secret chambers. Frea believes it has a connection to what's happening on Solstheim. I should read it to learn what secrets it holds.

After searching the Temple of Miraak, Frea and I found a strange book. When I read it, I was transported to some other realm, where I learned that Miraak is still alive and plans to return to Solstheim. I need to tell Frea what I've seen.

After finding Frea, and searching the Temple of Miraak, we discovered a strange book. When I read it, I was transported to some other realm and learned that Miraak is still alive and claims he'll return soon. Frea has suggested we take this information back to her village, and see what can be done to stop Miraak.

quests.name: The Fate of the Skaal
journal: After a strange experience with the Black Book in the Temple of Miraak, Frea says it is important to consult the Skaal Shaman. I should accompany her back to her village.

Storn, the Skaal shaman, has suggested that my experiences on Solstheim mean I am connected to Miraak. To follow the path Miraak has taken and learn what he knows, I must travel to Saering's Watch and learn the Word of Power written there.

In order to free the people of the Skaal, and to thwart Miraak's plans, I have learned a new Word of Power. I must use this new knowledge to disrupt the activity at the Wind Stone, where the Skaal are working against their will.
The people of the Skaal have been freed from the control they have been under, but in doing so a hideous creature has been released. It must be defeated before the Skaal are truly safe.

The Skaal have been freed from Miraak's control, and his minion has been destroyed. Now that Storn no longer needs to focus on keeping his people safe, he may be able to tell me more about how to find and defeat Miraak.

unsure.why: Narrative Gameplay Consistent Dialogue Tweaks puts a check on four opening lines (named for Aela's welcome): one of One-Handed, Two-Handed, Archery or Block at 30 or more, or Health or Stamina at 150 or more. Companions Dialogue Bundle takes it off and LoreRim - Dialogue Patch, later in load order, puts it back. The same mod adds two lines that only play if you're below all those marks and haven't finished The Horn of Jurgen Windcaller, Kindred Judgment, At the Summit of Apocrypha or Destroy the Dark Brotherhood!, which looks like a brush-off for untested newcomers that those quests let you skip. The line text isn't in these files, so whether this stops you joining is unsettled; Farkas, Skjor and Vilkas also have lines that send you to Kodlak.
Vilkas Spar Skip.esp loosens the conditions on a line tied to the spar with Vilkas, which suggests a way to skip the fight; the line text isn't in these files.

The Companions' shared script lists gold, Beast Form, Beastblood and a disabled Ring of Hircine power, and Companions Dialogue Bundle adds an 'Inspired' spell from Skjor's advice; none of these is tied to finishing this quest in the records. Vilkas's Sword and Aela's Shield are the quest items you carry.
The schedules send them to a training spot the records don't name (it's a marker, not a place); the yard behind Jorrvaskr, where Vilkas spars, is the likely spot.

Despite this, Tolfdir and I have explored further and found a strange orb buried deep within Saarthal. Tolfdir has asked that I take news of the discovery to the Arch-Mage.
I've delivered word to the Arch-Mage that something interesting was found deep within Saarthal.

quests.name: Revealing the Unseen
journal: I've been asked to speak with Mirabelle Ervine to follow up on the Staff of Magnus.

Mirabelle has told me that members of the Synod recently visited the College, mentioning the Staff of Magnus. They were last known to be heading towards Mzulft; they may know more about where to find the staff.

At Mirabelle's suggestion, I entered the ruins of Mzulft searching for the Synod researchers. I found one man who died, and suggested that more people may be inside at something called the Oculory. I should head further into the ruins to see what's going on.

At Mirabelle's suggestion, I entered the ruins of Mzulft searching for the Synod researchers. I found Paratus Decimius, who appears to be the only surviving member of the Synod expedition, and who has insisted that a "focusing crystal" is necessary to finish his experiment but was stolen by the Falmer.

Exploring Mzulft while looking for information about the Staff of Magnus, I've encountered Paratus Decimius, the sole surviving member of a Synod expedition. I've found the focusing crystal he needs to finish his experiment, and should return it to him.
Paratus Decimius may know the location of the Staff of Magnus, but has asked for my help in completing an experiment in Mzulft. I need to follow him to the top of the ruins.

Paratus Decimius may know the location of the Staff of Magnus, but has asked for my help in completing an experiment in Mzulft. I need to use magic to attenuate Paratus' focusing crystal, and then manipulate the dwarven machinery to line up the beams of light.

Traveling to Mzulft in search of the Synod, I found Paratus Decimius who helped me learn that the Staff of Magnus is located in Labyrinthian. This information needs to get back to Savos Aren at the College immediately.

After traveling to Mzulft and learning that the Staff of Magnus is located within Labyrinthian, I returned to the College to give the news to Arch-Mage Aren. Aren, however, is more concerned with the Eye of Magnus at the moment, since Ancano has locked himself in the Hall of the Elements with it. I need to help the Arch-Mage reach him at once.
After finding the Synod in Mzulft, I learned that the Staff of Magnus can be found in Labyrinthian, and brought this news to the Arch-Mage.

quests.name: Arniel's Endeavor
journal: Arniel has once again asked me to speak to Enthir, who was supposed to deliver something else relating to Arniel's project.

Arniel was convinced that Enthir was refusing to complete the trade the two of them had arranged, but it turns out that this time Enthir never received the item in question. The courier bringing the item never arrived. If I want to help Arniel finish his work, I'll need to find the courier myself.

Arniel was distraught over being unable to finish his project, believing that Enthir was refusing to complete a trade the two of them had agreed upon. Instead, the courier that was supposed to deliver the item never arrived. I've tracked him down (sadly he did not survive) and have the package Arniel wanted. I should make sure it gets to Arniel as soon as possible.

I've helped Arniel with the final piece of his project, by tracking down a missing courier who was supposed to be delivering an item from Morrowind. That item is Keening, a dwarven dagger that Arniel claims is very important. With it, he says he's able to finish his experiment and has asked that I observe what happens.
Arniel's experiment is over, but I'm not entirely sure what has happened. He has vanished, leaving behind the dagger Keening. I may never know whether he succeeded in his work.

quests.name: Enchanted To Meet You
journal: Sergius seems very busy, but he's offered to help me with enchanting. He's given me a note where the client orders are specified, but first I must find an enchanting table...

Sergius seemed very busy. I've offered to help him out with his Enchanting duties, as perhaps I can learn something in the process. He's given me a note where the client orders are described. First step will be disenchanting the old dagger he gave me, so I can learn its effects.

Sergius seemed very busy. I've offered to help him out with his Enchanting duties, as perhaps I can learn something in the process. It seems I need a filled gem to apply the enchantment the client wants.

Sergius seemed very busy. I've offered to help him out with his Enchanting duties, as perhaps I can learn something in the process. It seems I have a filled gem and I already know the enchantment the client wants, so I just need to apply it to the sword now.
I should show Sergius the enchantment, see if it's ready to be delivered.
Sergius has asked me to personally deliver the enchanted sword to the client. I should read the note he gave me to find out where this client is.
Sergius has asked me to personally deliver the enchanted sword to the client. I must find someone called Gretilde in Stonehills.
It turns out "the client" had nothing to do with the order. I should investigate before I leave Stonehills.

It turns out the client's daughter, Adara, sent the order to the College in the hopes of talking to a member of the College. She wants to be a mage and displays some aptitude already. I should talk to her.

It turns out the client's daughter, Adara, sent the order to the College in the hopes of talking to a member of the College. She wants to be a mage and displays some aptitude already. I'm not sure what to think, best talk to her mother.
Adara's mother has agreed to let her join the College of Winterhold. I'm to escort her and keep her safe until we get there.
Faralda won't let Adara join until she sees her magical aptitudes for herself. I should talk to the young mage.
That was quite the unusual delivery. I should talk to Sergius and explain what has happened.

Sergius taught me the basics of Enchanting and had work on my own enchantment.Things took a strange turn when I met a young mage called Adara while delivering the item. Sergius didn't care much for this though. It seems enchanting is quite the profitable business as it's keeping him quite busy. Now, that's an interesting lesson!
I refused to help Sergius with his enchanting, as he was clearly in a mood and I have no time to deal with people like him. Good riddance, I say.

read.about: The College of Winterhold is the mages' school in Winterhold; you join by casting a spell for Faralda at its entrance, and its story starts with an expedition to the ruins of Saarthal. The story has eight quests, with lessons, ritual spells and radiant jobs from the College's scholars alongside.

getIn.where: at the entrance to the College of Winterhold, in Winterhold
getIn.how: Talk to Faralda and cast the one spell she asks for: Magelight, a Flame Atronach, Firebolt, Fear, or Healing Hands on her.

Recover the books Orthorn stole for Urag gro-Shub from Fellglow Keep.
Tell Tolfdir about the Night of Tears book, meet Quaranir of the Psijic Order and find the Augur of Dunlain in the Midden.

journal: Brynjolf has promised me more work if I'm able to locate him at a tavern called the Ragged Flagon. Judging from the dangerous nature of its location, it seems as though he's having me perform some type of initiation, but I can't be certain.

After successfully locating the Ragged Flagon, Brynjolf has given me a new assignment. Three business owners in Riften are proving to be a thorn in his side and I'm supposed to teach them the error of their ways. I should speak to Brynjolf about these townspeople in the event that they prove to be as stubborn as I'm expecting them to be.

I've dealt with the three troublesome business owners in Riften as Brynjolf had specified. Perhaps now that I've proven my worth to Brynjolf, I can discover more about this mysterious organization that he represents.

quests.name: Loud and Clear
journal: Brynjolf is taking me to meet the leader of the organization he represents. He says more work and significantly more coin could be available if I join their ranks.
Thanks to Brynjolf's support, I've been welcomed into the Thieves Guild by its Guild Master, Mercer Frey. I'm eager to receive my first task and prove that his recommendation wasn't in vain.

My first task as a member of the Thieves Guild involves a honey operation located just outside of Riften called Goldenglow Estate. My actions there are in direct response to the owner's sudden silence and lack of cooperation with the Thieves Guild and Maven-Black-Briar, one of the Guild's most important clients.

I've completed my task at Goldenglow Estate and discovered the owner's sudden lack of cooperation with the Guild was leveraged by an anonymous buyer of that very same location. Why this buyer purchased Goldenglow and is showing animosity towards the Guild is a mystery for the moment.

quests.name: Dampened Spirits
journal: I've been sent to speak to Maven Black-Briar, head of the wealthiest most influential family in Riften. According to Brynjolf, she has a job of utmost importance for me and I need to follow her directions to the letter.

Maven Black-Briar has sent me to Whiterun where I am to meet with someone named Mallus Maccius. Together, our goal is to bring down one of Maven's competitors, Honningbrew Meadery and discover where he obtained the financing to take her on.

I've become a key component in a cunning plan to frame Honningbrew Meadery's owner, Sabjorn, and have him imprisoned. The first part of the scheme is to approach Sabjorn under the guise of assistance with a pest problem he's having thanks to Mallus's tinkering.

Sabjorn has provided me with poison I'm to apply to the nests deep within the tunnels under Honningbrew Meadery. As Mallus predicted, I should be able to use the very same poison to taint Sabjorn's mead as well.
The plan worked perfectly and Whiterun's Captain of the Guard was stricken with illness when he drank the poisoned mead. Sabjorn's been carted off to jail and Honningbrew Meadery is now closed.
Now that Mallus's position as the owner of Honningbrew Meadery has been secured, I need to find any information explaining how Sabjorn was able to fund this costly operation.

The information I obtained from Honningbrew Meadery points to the same anonymous buyer of Goldenglow Estate. If successful, this individual would have completely estranged Maven Black-Briar from the Guild and destroyed it economically. It's becoming painfully obvious that it's time to shed some light on our mysterious adversary before they have a chance to strike again.

quests.name: Scoundrel's Folly
journal: After the revelations at Honningbrew Meadery and Goldenglow Farm, it's time to put the pieces together and shed some light on the Thieves Guild's anonymous adversary.

Mercer Frey has pointed to Solitude as my next destination. I'm to meet up with an old Argonian contact for the Guild named Gulum-Ei. It's hoped he'll be able to identify the Thieves Guild's anonymous adversary.

As predicted by Mercer Frey, Gulum-Ei proved to be quite stubborn and refused to reveal any useful information. I have no choice but to shadow him during his daily routine and discover if he's up to anything that could be used as influence to make him divulge the truth.

Thanks to Gulum-Ei's confession, a former member of the Thieves Guild named Karliah has been identified as its anonymous adversary. Worse still, I've discovered that she was the same Dunmer who murdered Gallus, the Guild's previous Guild Master and who's apparently resurfaced after all these years to do the same to Mercer Frey.

quests.name: Speaking With Silence
journal: I'm on my way to meet Mercer Frey at the ruins of Snow Veil Sanctum, Karliah's last known location. Together, Mercer and I intend to hunt her down and make her pay for Gallus' murder.

The tables have unexpectedly turned, and Mercer Frey has been revealed as Gallus' killer. I now find myself in Karliah's care after Mercer tried to murder me, claiming I'd outlasted my usefulness by witnessing their conversation. I've also discovered that Mercer, Gallus, and Karliah were members of some sort of group calling themselves "The Nightingales" - guardians in service to the goddess Nocturnal. What they're protecting or what this has to do with the Guild is still a mystery to me.

journal: Karliah believes the only proof that could expose Mercer's treachery can be found within the pages of Gallus' journal which she recovered from Snow Veil Sanctum. Unfortunately, the journal is written in some sort of code that needs to be deciphered. Our only hope is Enthir, one of Karliah and Gallus' former acquaintances who is a wizard at the College of Winterhold.

Enthir has informed me that Gallus' journal is written in Falmer. He's directed me to seek out Calcelmo, the court wizard in Markarth who is the foremost authority on them in hopes of obtaining a translation.

Calcelmo has proven to be extremely stubborn and refuses to allow me access to his materials regarding the Falmer language. I'm left with little choice other than taking matters into my own hands and stealing his notes.

Calcelmo's "notes" on the Falmer language are actually derived from a massive stone slab in his tower! It will be impossible to bring this item to Enthir to have him translate Gallus' journal. I'll have to discover a way to make the information more portable.

After Enthir successfully translated Gallus' journal, I've discovered that Mercer's motivations transcended simple greed or murder. As a member of the Nightingales, Mercer was tasked with guarding a place called the Twilight Sepulcher, the Temple of Nocturnal. According to Gallus, he defiled the temple and betrayed the Thieves Guild. Karliah insists we bring this information to Brynjolf immediately.

quests.name: The Pursuit
journal: I'm on my way back to the Ragged Flagon to meet up with Karliah. Using the information obtained from Gallus' journal as proof, I hope to convince Brynjolf of Karliah's innocence and Mercer Frey's betrayal.

Brynjolf has been convinced of Karliah's innocence and Mercer's betrayal after investigating the Guild's treasure vault and finding it empty. Of greater mystery is the fact that the vault can only be opened with two keys and is utterly impervious to lockpicking. How Mercer Frey could have breached it is a mystery to us all.
The hunt is on and I'm on my way to Riftweald Manor, Mercer Frey's estate in Riften, to locate a clue as to his current whereabouts.
I've discovered some plans in Riftweald Manor. This must be where Mercer Frey is headed. I should bring these to Brynjolf as soon as possible.

Brynjolf is convinced Mercer Frey intends to perform one final heist before departing Skyrim for good. According to the plans I discovered in Riftweald Manor, he's after the "Eyes of the Falmer," two gems of enormous value. If we have any hopes of intercepting Mercer, we need to proceed to their location immediately.

quests.name: Trinity Restored
journal: Before intercepting Mercer Frey, Karliah wishes to speak to both Brynjolf and myself.

Karliah has indicated Brynjolf and I are to meet her at an old standing stone just outside the Southwest Gate of Riften. Her motivations for doing so are mysterious, but I suspect it has something to do with the Nightingales.

Karliah has informed Brynjolf and I that we're to join the elite ranks of the Nightingales and assist in reforming the trinity that was disrupted over twenty-five years ago when Mercer Frey murdered Gallus.
I've undertaken the Oath and I'm now a Nightingale, guardian of the Twilight Sepulcher and a dedicated sentinel of the goddess Nocturnal.

Karliah has finally revealed the fundamental mission of the Nightingales... the guardianship of the Skeleton Key of Nocturnal. This powerful artifact, normally kept safely within the Twilight Sepulcher, has been stolen by Mercer Frey. As a Nightingale, the duty to recover the Skeleton Key falls squarely upon my shoulders.

quests.name: Blindsighted
journal: I'm on my way to Irkngthand, a vast dwarven ruin that supposedly contains the legendary "Eyes of the Falmer." Karliah and Brynjolf are waiting for me within. Together we hope to stop Mercer Frey from stealing the Eyes and escaping from Skyrim with the Skeleton Key of Nocturnal.

I've entered Irkngthand, a vast dwarven ruin that supposedly contains the legendary "Eyes of the Falmer." Karliah and Brynjolf are waiting for me within. Together we hope to stop Mercer Frey from stealing the Eyes and escaping from Skyrim with the Skeleton Key of Nocturnal.

Karliah and Brynjolf have joined me in my exploration of Irkngthand, a vast dwarven ruin that supposedly contains the legendary "Eyes of the Falmer." Together we hope to stop Mercer Frey from stealing the Eyes and escaping from Skyrim with the Skeleton Key of Nocturnal.
I've finally located Mercer Frey within the ruins of Irkngthand. He seemed to be expecting us, and I'm afraid he led us here with the express purpose of eliminating the Nightingales once and for all.

Mercer Frey, betrayer of the Thieves Guild and Gallus' murderer is finally dead. Upon his death, a wave of magic issued from his body and has caused the already crumbling chamber to collapse and fill with water.
Mercer Frey is dead and I've recovered the Skeleton Key of Nocturnal from his corpse. I need to escape Irkngthand before the place collapses around me.

Safe from the dangers below, Karliah, Brynjolf, and I finally have a moment to breathe. Mercer Frey is dead, the Skeleton Key of Nocturnal is in my possession and, most importantly, the Nightingales have survived.

Karliah, Brynjolf, and I have slain Mercer Frey, escaped Irkngthand, and recovered the Skeleton Key. All that remains is returning the artifact to the Twilight Sepulcher where it belongs; a journey I must undertake alone.

quests.name: Darkness Returns
journal: With the Skeleton Key of Nocturnal safely in my possession, I'm bound for the Twilight Sepulcher to return it to its resting place.

Within the Twilight Sepulcher, I happened upon the spirit of Gallus, the Nightingale murdered by Mercer Frey. He warned me that removing the key from its resting place has corrupted the other resident Nightingale Guardian Spirits, distorting their morality and making them incredibly hostile.

I've returned the Skeleton Key to its proper resting place within the Twilight Sepulcher and encountered Nocturnal herself. As a reward for my actions, she allowed me to become a true Nightingale Agent and imbued me with the appropriate ability befitting my station.

journal: It was suggested that I show my Unusual Gem to Vex, a member of the Thieves Guild in Riften. However, I'll need to wait until I'm a full member of the Guild before she'll be able to assist me.
I've found an unusual gem which seems to exhibit magical properties. I should bring it to Vex at the Thieves Guild for an appraisal.
The unusual gem has turned out to be one of twenty-four "Stones of Barenziah." According to Vex, they have little value unless the set is complete.

Vex has revealed to me that the Crown of Barenziah is actually a paragon for the Thieves Guild. If I can recover the crown from Tolvald's Cave, she should be able to restore our paragon to its full strength.
I've brought the Crown of Barenziah back to Vex, who has restored it to its original condition where it now serves as a paragon for the Thieves Guild.

quests.name: Summerset Shadows
journal: Torsten Cruel-Sea, a wealthy merchant residing in Windhelm, has requested assistance from the Thieves Guild.

Torsten Cruel-Sea's daughter Fjotli was slain and robbed of a silver locket by a Thieves Guild hailing from Summerset Isle. Calling themselves "The Summerset Shadows," they are looking into expanding their influence in Skyrim.

Torsten's daughter wasn't slain by the Summerset Shadows, but their leader, Linwe, has them robbing the dead of their valuables. Linwe and the rest of his guild have established a hideout in Uttering Hills Cave.
I've slain Linwe and obtained Fjotli's Silver Locket. This ends the presence of the Summerset Shadows in Skyrim.
The locket has been returned to Torsten Cruel-Sea, and the Thieves Guild can now count on him as an influential ally in Windhelm.

read.about: The Thieves Guild is a guild of thieves based in the Ragged Flagon and the Cistern under Riften, and its story has you rise through the guild while it searches for a hidden enemy. The main story runs eleven quests, from A Chance Arrangement to Darkness Returns, with city jobs, collection quests and radiant jobs for Vex and Delvin Mallory around it.

getIn.where: outdoors in Riften
getIn.how: Talk to Brynjolf in Riften; he talks you into one of his schemes and tells you to meet him during the day.

order.what: You steal Madesi's Silver Ring and plant it for Brynjolf.
You find Brynjolf in the Ragged Flagon and collect three debts for the guild from Keerava, Bersi and Haelga.
You meet Mercer Frey, the Guild Master, and are sent to burn three bee hives and empty Aringoth's safe at Goldenglow Estate.
order.where: the Cistern under Riften and Goldenglow Estate, just outside Riften

You meet Mercer outside Snow Veil Sanctum to hunt down Karliah.
Karliah needs Gallus' journal read, which sends you to Enthir at the College of Winterhold and then to Markarth.
order.where: the College of Winterhold and Understone Keep in Markarth

order.what: You meet Karliah at the Ragged Flagon, convince the guild, and break into Riftweald Manor for Mercer's plans.
order.where: the Ragged Flagon and Riftweald Manor in Riften

Only if you break one of the guild's rules and are banned: you pay Vex to be let back in.

quests.name: Innocence Lost
journal: I heard a rumor that a boy named Aventus Aretino, in Windhelm, has been attempting to contact the Dark Brotherhood. I should find this boy and speak with him, and find out why he wants to contact a guild of assassins.

The mother of Aventus Aretino recently died, and the boy was sent to live at Honorhall Orphanage in Riften. He thinks I'm a Dark Brotherhood assassin, and wants me to kill the Orphanage's sadistic headmistress, Grelod the Kind. I could kill her or talk to the guards in Riften to try and have her arrested.
I've convinced Grelod the Kind that Aventus Aretino is just outside Riften. She's agreed to follow me to the docks, where I can then get rid of her discreetly.
Grelod is at the docks, where no one can see her. Time to get rid of her.
Grelod the kind has been dealt with. I should inform Aventus.
I should check on the children at the Honorhall Orphanage now that Grelod is spending the rest of her days at Riften's jail.
It turns out Grelod was killed while imprisoned. Perhaps Aventus Aretino actually managed to summon the Dark Brotherhood after all.
I killed Grelod the Kind, and Aventus Aretino rewarded me with a family heirloom. Now the boy can return to Honorhall Orphanage, and live out his childhood peacefully.

quests.name: With Friends Like These...
journal: Astrid, of the Dark Brotherhood, informed me that by killing Grelod the Kind, I have robbed her organization of a kill. I have been taken captive and moved to some remote shack. Astrid will only give me the key if I kill someone she has taken captive, to "repay my debt."

I have killed one of the captives as Astrid instructed, and must now gain entrance to the Dark Brotherhood Sanctuary, which is located in the southern Pine Forest. Astrid has provided me with the correct passphrase - "Silence, my Brother."

quests.name: The Silence Has Been Broken
journal: I returned to Nazir, but he directed me to speak with Astrid immediately. Perhaps she's made up her mind about me seeing Amaund Motierre in Volundruud.
Astrid has agreed to let me see Amaund Motierre in the dungeon known as Volunruud, as commanded by the Night Mother. I'm to speak with Motierre, and find out what he wants.

Amaund Motierre has commissioned the Dark Brotherhood to kill several people, all of which will lead to the assassination of a primary target - the Emperor of Tamriel himself. I am to report this information back to Astrid.

I've given Astrid the amulet and sealed letter provided to me by Amaund Motierre. I'm to take the amulet to a fence named Delvin Mallory, in the Riften Ratway - to gain any information I can, and sell it if Mallory is willing to buy.

Delvin Mallory has informed me that the amulet provided by Amaund Motierre indicates he is a member of the Emperor's Elder Council. Mallory was willing to purchase the amulet in exchange for a letter of credit, which I must now deliver to Astrid.
After meeting with Amaund Motierre, I learned he is a member of the Elder Council, and wants the Dark Brotherhood to kill several people, all of whom lead to a primary target - the Emperor himself.

journal: I must speak with Festus Krex about my next target, the renowned chef known only as the "Gourmet."

I have been tasked with killing the Gourmet, but only one person knows the famous chef's true identity and location - a man named Anton Virane. I must get this information from Anton Virane, and then kill him.
I must kill the Gourmet, who is actually an Orc named Balagog gro-Nolob. Once he's dead, I must steal his Writ of Passage. And, if I can manage to hide the body, I'll receive a bonus.
The Gourmet is dead, and I'm now in possession of his Writ of Passage. Soon, I will take his place as chef for the Emperor...

quests.name: To Kill an Empire
journal: It would appear all the contracts leading up to the Emperor's assassination have been completed. I must now speak with Astrid, and receive further instructions.

Using the Writ of Passage issued to the chef known as "The Gourmet," I must enter Castle Dour and play the part of the culinary master, who is scheduled to prepare a feast. This will be my opportunity to assassinate the Emperor, using any tools at my disposal.

It was a trap! The Emperor was actually Titus Mede II's double, and Commander Maro said I had been betrayed by someone within the Dark Brotherhood. Despite his deal, Maro has sent troops to destroy the Sanctuary. I must return there and help my Family!

After learning the Emperor was actually Titus Mede II's double, and being confronted by Commander Maro, I learned Maro had betrayed the betrayer, and sent troops to destroy the Dark Brotherhood Sanctuary. I returned there, to lend aid to my fellow Family members.

read.about: The Dark Brotherhood is a guild of assassins based in a Sanctuary in the pine forest near Falkreath, and its story has you take contracts across Skyrim that build toward one great contract. The main story runs thirteen quests, from Innocence Lost to Hail Sithis!, with many side contracts around it.

read.about: The Vigilant line follows the Vigilants of Stendarr, an order based at the Temple of Stendarr in their own land of Stuhn Ravine, as you hunt vampires, Daedra and witches across Skyrim with Altano and later go into Coldharbour. Its first act runs eleven quests, from Vigilant of Stendarr to The Landing, followed by a vampire hunt under Windhelm, the Coldharbour memories, and bounties and radiant hunts on the side.

getIn.how: The quest starts on its own the next time you enter or leave a place; Altano invites you to join the Vigilants of Stendarr and offers to guide you to the Temple of Stendarr.

the first act's order comes from the series numbering and each first objective sending you to where the last quest ended; no condition in the files ties one quest to the next
who hands out the bounties and the Radiance jobs, and whether you must have joined first, isn't in the files
what starts Empty Cells, the Coldharbour memories, Broken Horns, Maggot, Child of Oblivion and Successor isn't in the files; Empty Cells probably follows the first act

The Landing and Art of Mercy both unlock the Rusty Armor recipes, which suggests they are alternate endings of the first act after No Mercy, but nothing in the files says one locks out the other or which No Mercy choice leads where

most rewards are properties on quest scripts, not confirmed hand-overs; Lamae's Kin and Mark of Molag Bal may be given or lifted by several quests, and spells like Force, Eye of Madness and Vampire Form may be effects used in a scene rather than rewards
whether Lamae Bal dies in The Blood Matron, and what happens to Thingol in Remnants, isn't in the files

quests.name: Infiltration
journal: Returning from securing the staff 'Summoner's Demise', Alara told me to speak to Laracin, who is spearheading a plan to infiltrate a group of Necromancers.

Returning from securing the staff 'Summoner's Demise', Alara told me to speak to Laracin, who is spearheading a plan to infiltrate a group of Necromancers. He has sent me to Deep Moon Lookout to meet with a recruiter for the Necromancers - where he has recommended I do whatever it takes to join the Necromancers.

In order to infiltrate the Dark Dawn, a group of Necromancers, the recruiter Dralos has told me to kill a woman named Adelaide. I must make a choice whether to kill her, attempt to reason with them, or kill the Necromancers and find another way to infiltrate the group.

In order to infiltrate the Dark Dawn, a group of Necromancers, the recruiter Dralos told me to kill a woman named Adelaide. However, I made the choice to kill the Necromancers. I should speak with Adelaide to find out what she knows about the group.

In order to infiltrate the Dark Dawn, a group of Necromancers, the recruiter Dralos told me to kill a woman named Adelaide. I made the choice to kill her, and must now speak with Dralos in order to find out the location of their sanctuary.
I have discovered the location of the Dark Dawn Sanctuary. I must make my way there and gain access to the Sanctuary in order to find evidence of their plans.

I have gained access to the Dark Dawn Sanctuary. I must search for a way to find out what these Necromancers are planning. I could try searching through secret documents, gaining the favor of members of the group, or fighting my way through to their plans.

I have discovered that the Necromancers are planning to raise the First Vampire created by Molag Bal. I must return to Alara and inform her of this information, or see if I can find out anything more about the Dark Dawn.

Upon returning to Meridia's Sanctum, I have found it to be attacked by the group named The Malevolent and Acolyte Kariss has been killed. I must speak with Alara to find out what I can do to help this situation.

quests.name: The Jester, In The Bedroom, With The Knife
journal: I have been approached by a Wood Elf known simply as The Jester. Enduring misery, she has asked me to help her destroy the realm. Jester has asked me to find evidence that Fiya is plotting against her or Alzacar, a loyal servant to the Dark Master. If I can find evidence, The Jester is certain Alzacar will help us destroy the realm.

I have been approached by a Wood Elf known simply as The Jester. Enduring misery, she has asked me to help her destroy the realm. Jester has asked me to find evidence that Fiya is plotting against her or Alzacar, and I have done so. Alzacar has agreed to help us destroy the realm, but I must first kill Kelrog, a fierce and loyal advisor to Fiya who may stand in our way.

I have been approached by a Wood Elf known simply as The Jester. Enduring misery, she has asked me to help her destroy the realm. Jester has asked me to find evidence that Fiya is plotting against her or Alzacar, and I have done so. Alzacar has agreed to help us destroy the realm, but I first had to kill Kelrog, a fierce and loyal advisor to Fiya who might have stood in our way. I should return to Alzacar to gain knowledge on how to destroy this place.
I have gained the information that I need. Outlandish like Garin said, the way to destroy this realm is through killing a conjured dog named Molag. Alzacar said I can find him in the Master Bedroom.
I have burned my bridges with The Jester and Alzacar. I may have to find another way to gain the information I need to destroy this place.

read.about: A mod-added story line in which you join Meridia's Order, a band of Meridia's followers led by High Priestess Alara, and work against a group of necromancers across Skyrim. It has nine story quests that begin at Meridia's Sanctum and later move to Fort Justice in the Rift, three side quests along the way, and five quests for members of the Order once the story is done.

The mod has a 'Legion requirement met' setting that starts off, so joining may need something to do with the Imperial Legion; and its jobs hunt 'escaped' Dark Brotherhood members, which suggests it expects the Brotherhood to have been destroyed. Neither is confirmed.
The armour is held by the quest's script; that it is handed over on joining is the likely reading, not confirmed.
Maro is also the giver of the line's repeatable jobs (a second Unfinished Business, House Cleaning, Paperwork, Inquisition, Troubleshoot); what unlocks them isn't in these files.
Maro uses a stay-where-placed package, so the outpost should be right, but that package is shared by many people.
Maro is a target in the Dark Brotherhood's own quests (To Kill an Empire, Hail Sithis!); how that clashes with this line isn't in the records.

read.about: A mod-added line in which you join the Penitus Oculatus, the Empire's security force and the Emperor's bodyguards, and hunt down Dark Brotherhood members who are still at large. Commander Maro at the Penitus Oculatus Outpost in Dragon Bridge takes you in, hands out the assignments and takes your reports: five story missions after joining, and five radiant assignments.

getIn.where: the Penitus Oculatus Outpost in Dragon Bridge
getIn.how: Talk to Commander Maro and join the Penitus Oculatus; from then on you ask him for assignments.

order.what: Join the Penitus Oculatus through Commander Maro.
Maro's first assignment: deal with an escaped Dark Brotherhood assassin hiding at the Moorside Inn and learn where Cicero and Babette are.
Track down and kill Babette, then report to Maro.
order.needs: Learn where Babette is in Unfinished Business

order.what: Track down and kill Cicero, read his journal, then report to Maro.
order.needs: Learn where Cicero is in Unfinished Business

order.what: Use the passphrase from Cicero's journal to get into the Dawnstar Sanctuary, clear it out and read the Listener's Journal.
order.needs: Finish Fool's Errand

order.what: Kill Amaund Motierre at Volunruud and report to Maro.
A radiant assignment from Maro: kill an escaped Dark Brotherhood assassin at a place named in your journal.
A radiant assignment from Maro: kill three rogue Penitus Oculatus agents at a place named in your journal.
A radiant assignment from Maro: take documents from a Thalmor agent without getting tangled up with the hold's authorities.
A radiant assignment from Maro: kill a noble who is secretly working for the Aldmeri Dominion without getting tangled up with the hold's authorities.
A radiant assignment from Maro: kill a Thalmor agent who is interfering with Penitus Oculatus operations, without getting tangled up with the hold's authorities.

options: Kill the assassin and search her body for intel
Let her defect, escort her to the outpost in Dragon Bridge and read the Listener's Orders she gives you; she later joins the agents in the Dawnstar Sanctuary

gives: Penitus Oculatus Cuirass, Bracers, Helmet and Boots, on joining
Gold from Commander Maro for each mission and assignment
Items the quest sets in the Dawnstar Sanctuary in A Nest of Vipers, among them Windshear, Nightweaver's Band, Firiniel's End and Muiri's Ring
closes: The Dark Brotherhood Defector, if you kill her in Unfinished Business
Babette dies in Bad Blood
Cicero dies in Fool's Errand
The Dark Brotherhood's Listener and five assassins in the Dawnstar Sanctuary are killed; Penitus Oculatus agents move in afterwards
Amaund Motierre dies in Loose Ends

unsure.why: No level is given for any quest in the line, and how long it takes isn't in the records.

The conditions on Maro's joining line aren't in these files. The mod has a 'Legion requirement met' setting that starts off, so joining may need something to do with the Imperial Legion; its jobs hunt 'escaped' Dark Brotherhood members, which suggests it expects the Brotherhood to have been destroyed. Neither is confirmed.
Commander Maro is a target in the Dark Brotherhood's own quests (To Kill an Empire, Hail Sithis!); how this line clashes with the Dark Brotherhood line isn't in the records.

unsure.field: order.Bad Blood / Fool's Errand / A Nest of Vipers / Loose Ends
unsure.why: No giver line or script that starts these is in these files; each is tied to the one before by its journal text. Whether A Nest of Vipers also needs Bad Blood done isn't shown, and where Babette and Cicero hide is filled in at run time.

Maro's offer lines for the five assignments are in the records but their conditions aren't, so it's not known whether they wait for the story missions. One of them shares the name Unfinished Business with the Moorside Inn mission.

The armour is held by the joining quest's script and is likely handed over on joining, not confirmed. Gold amounts aren't in these files. The Dawnstar Sanctuary items come from the quest's item slots; whether they're loot, on display or on a mannequin isn't shown.

journal: I am to lead someone to the Shrine of Boethiah, instruct them to touch the Pillar of Sacrifice, and once trapped by its magic, slay them. If I do this Boethiah will appear.
Boethiah has appeared using the person the job names's corpse as a vessel. She will give a special task to whichever of her cultists are left alive after we fight to the death.

Boethiah revealed herself to me. I am to slay her previous champion, and having done so, don the Ebony Mail. So doing, she will make me her champion. Her former champion stays within a bandit-occupied mine in the mountains northwest of Falkreath.
I have proven myself to Boethiah, and she has made me her new champion.

After slaying her cultists, Boethiah appeared to me.  She desired that I sacrifice a follower in order to prove myself to her, but I refused to take any part in such a vile act. As punishment, she has cursed me.  I should pray to the Divines and hope that they will remove the curse.
Stendarr has granted me the Gauntlets of the Crusader as a reward for refusing Boethiah's wishes.
I have slain Boethiah's cultists; Molag Bal should be pleased.  I should visit his altar in Markarth to see if he will grant me greater power as a reward for this victory over his enemy.
Molag Bal has granted me the Hands of Coldharbour as a reward for my victory over Boethiah's followers.

quests.name: The Man in Black
journal: I have agreed to help Rudin Filaro, a Dark Elf intent on visiting the Temple of Mara located in the mountains northeast of Kynesgrove. He has hired to escort him as the road is known to be dangerous.

I was betrayed! Upon entering the mountain pass, a rune set by the Dark Elf left me paralyzed. I have just regained consciousness hours later, barely alive, next to a shrine of Boethiah. I must investigate the area to discover what has transpired here.

The Dark Elf lured me here to sacrifice me to Boethiah, the Daedric Prince of Deception. Miraculously, I survived the ritual the cultists performed. The elf is now traveling to Knifepoint Ridge to kill a dangerous man whom the Prince wants dead.

I tracked Rudin Filaro to Knifepoint Ridge. I found him standing over the previous Champion of Boethiah's corpse, whose title the elf had now claimed. After a palaver, our fight to the death commenced. I emerged victorious, marking an end to his exploits.

quests.name: Discerning the Transmundane
journal: I've been given a book of bizarre ramblings about Elder Scrolls, written by Septimus Signus. He claims to have spent time at the Winterhold Arcanaeum.
I've learned that Septimus Signus, a preeminent scholar of the Elder Scrolls, is currently living in the far north, studying a dwarven artifact. He might know where I can find an Elder Scroll.

I met Septimus Signus, a brilliant but mad scholar living in the northern ice fields. He's directed me to a dwarven observatory that supposedly houses an Elder Scroll. He doesn't care about the Scroll itself, but wants me to use some kind of machine there to inscribe a dwarven lexicon with the Scroll's knowledge and bring it to him.

I met Septimus Signus and brought him a dwarven lexicon containing the distilled knowledge of an Elder Scroll. With it, he believes he can open the lockbox he's been studying. He will contact me when he has the secret.

I met Septimus Signus and brought him a dwarven lexicon containing the distilled knowledge of an Elder Scroll. With it, he believes he can open the lockbox he's been studying by creating a mixture of blood that will resemble dwarven. I need to collect blood from several different races if I want to help him.

I met a strange hermit named Septimus Signus, who needed the knowledge of an Elder Scroll and a collection of blood to open a dwarven lockbox he had studied for years. I helped him open it. It did not contain what he had expected, but instead a book of great knowledge, the Oghma Infinium.
I met and killed a strange hermit named Septimus Signus, who needed the knowledge of an Elder Scroll and a collection of blood to open a dwarven lockbox he had studied for years.
