quests.name: The Cursed Tribe
journal: I've heard rumors there's some kind of problem in the Orc settlement of Largashbur, southwest of Riften.
The Orcs of Largashbur are besieged by giants. Atub, the wise woman of the tribe, has asked me to talk the chief, Yamarz.

The Orcs of Largashbur are besieged by giants. The chief, Yamarz, told me that he has been cursed by ghosts haunting him, leaving him and the tribe weak and vulnerable to Giant attacks. He asked me to petition Malacath to remove the curse.

The Orcs of Largashbur are besieged by giants. The chief, Yamarz, told me that he has been cursed by ghosts haunting him, leaving him and the tribe weak and vulnerable to Giant attacks. I told him I know a spell that could help him.

The Orcs of Largashbur are besieged by giants. The chief, Yamarz, told me that he has been cursed by ghosts haunting him, leaving him and the tribe weak and vulnerable to Giant attacks. Atub told me there should be shrine of Malacath northwest of Largushbur.

The Orcs of Largashbur are besieged by giants. The chief, Yamarz, told me that he has been cursed by ghosts haunting him, leaving him and the tribe weak and vulnerable to Giant attacks. I located the shrine northwest of Largashbur. I was unable to contact Malacath, but found a note on an Orc skeleton mentioning Yamarz should "listen with the ears of the wind".

The Orcs of Largashbur are besieged by giants, and have been forbidden to leave their stronghold. Atub, the wise woman of the tribe, has asked me to find her troll fat and a Daedra heart so that she may contact Malacath for guidance.

The Orcs of Largashbur are besieged by giants. The chief, Yamarz, told me that he has been cursed by ghosts haunting him, leaving him and the tribe weak and vulnerable to Giant attacks. I've cast a spell to make the ghosts appear and they're now attacking the stronghold.

The Orcs of Largashbur are besieged by giants. The chief, Yamarz, told me that he has been cursed by ghosts haunting him, leaving him and the tribe weak and vulnerable to Giant attacks. I've cast a spell to make the ghosts appear and defeated them.

The Orcs of Largashbur are besieged by giants. The chief, Yamarz, told me that he has been cursed by ghosts haunting him, leaving him and the tribe weak and vulnerable to Giant attacks. I've cast a spell to make the ghosts appear and defeated them.

Malacath has spoken to his followers and expressed disappointment in them. He is angry they allowed his shrine to be desecrated, and has commanded the chieftain of Largashbur, Yamarz, to return to the shrine and reclaim it.

Despite being specifically instructed by Malacath to see to it himself, Yamarz wants my help in defeating the giants that have overrun Fallowstone Cave and the shrine of Malacath. He's promised to pay me in exchange for making sure he arrives there safely.

After Malacath ordered him to retake the shrine in Fallowstone Cave, Yamarz insisted that I escort him there to make sure he arrived safely. Now he has offered to pay me even more in exchange for killing the giant myself, to which I have agreed.

After Malacath ordered him to retake the shrine in Fallowstone Cave, Yamarz insisted that I escort him there to make sure he arrived safely. He offered to pay me even more in exchange for killing the giant myself, but I declined. Yamarz died trying to fight the giant, so I suppose it's up to me now.
After escorting Yamarz to Fallowstone Cave and proving myself more worthy, Malacath has commanded me to return to Largashbur and deliver Shagrol's Hammer there.

The curse placed on the Orcs of Largashbur is lifted. The tribe's leader, Yamarz, was revealed as a shiftless weakling in Malacath's eyes, and I have redeemed his actions by defeating the giant that had taken over the shrine in Fallowstone Cave. Malacath has named Gularzob as the new chief, and has named me his new champion.
Using magic, I've helped the Orc Stronghold of Largashbur get rid of the ghosts that were haunting their chief.

unsure.why: The quest also has a level-up start (the rumor); its level isn't decoded here. Burguk's and Mauhulakh's opening lines exist but their words aren't in these files. Their daytime packages have no place, so only the hour is known. Atub's waking package is a sandbox around a spot with no named cell (most likely outdoors); only her sleep spot is the longhouse.

The shrine northwest of Largashbur is the Orc skeleton's spot, which is out in the open world; the place the records call the Sanctum of Malacath shares Fallowstone Cave's map marker, so it is the giants' grove inside the cave, not the shrine with the skeleton. The direction comes from Atub's line and the journal.

Getting the spell choice and some talk with Yamarz and Ugor depend on speech checks and other conditions that aren't fully decoded here; that you need to know Bane of the Undead is read from the objective, not from a condition.

Volendrung and the necklace are script properties; which ending gives which isn't spelled out, and two other completing endings have no journal text. Yamarz promises to pay you for the escort, but no gold is named in the records. The script's giant-club Shagrol's Warhammer isn't a playable item, so it is left out.
The objective says Garok Longstride; the giant's own record is named Gorak Longstride.

journal: A strange Argonian in the marsh has offered to teach me how to smith madness ore in exchange for retriving a "treasure" from some nearby ruins. I should head there now.

A strange Argonian in the marsh offered to teach me how to smith madness ore in exchange for retriving a "treasure" from some nearby ruins. I found a strange crystalline artifact in the ruin. I should return to the Argonian.

A strange Argonian in the marsh offered to teach me how to smith madness ore in exchange for retriving a "treasure" from some nearby ruins. quests.name: Waking Nightmare
journal: I've overheard two citizens of Dawnstar complaining about horrible nightmares. They seem to be relying on a priest of Mara named Erandur for assistance.

Erandur has assured me he can end the nightmares, the source of which seems to be within Nightcaller Temple, a place of worship for Vaermina. I have agreed to assist him in this endeavor and we are now on our way.

Erandur has revealed that Nightcaller Temple contains the legendary Skull of Corruption, an artifact of great power. In order to end the nightmares, we must breach the inner sanctum and allow Erandur to perform a ritual on the Skull which will render it inert.

From a tome obtained in the temple's library, Erandur has discovered a way to breach the inner sanctum. By obtaining a special liquid, we'll be able to perform a Dreamstride... travel a distance using another subject's dreams.

With Vaermina's Torpor in hand, I am ready to undergo the Dreamstride. I must drink the liquid which will enable me to enter the dreams of those who still slumber within these walls and use them to breach the inner sanctum.

I've found myself within the dreams of a priest of Vaermina. I am experiencing the Orc invasion of the temple over a decade ago. In the guise of the priest, I've been tasked with releasing the Miasma and placing everyone inside the temple in a deep sleep.
After awakening from the Dreamstride, I was able to remove the barrier to the inner sanctum. I must now follow Erandur to the Skull of Corruption so it can be rendered inert.

I've heard the words of the goddess Vaermina, who claims that Erandur will kill me after the ritual to destroy the Skull of Corruption is complete. I must make a choice; either allow Erandur to complete the ritual and destroy the Skull, or kill Erandur and wield the Skull of Corruption as my own.
I've made my decision, and allowed Erandur to live. The Skull of Corruption has been destroyed and Erandur has offered his services as a companion if I should ever need his assistance.
I've made my decision and Erandur has died by my hands. Unfortunately, the Skull of Corruption was destroyed before I could take his life. Such moments are the misfortunes of the indecisive.
I've made my decision and Erandur has died by my hands. I now possess the Skull of Corruption and look forward to performing my duties for Lady Vaermina.

Goreduster's location isn't in these files; the bandit's journal says it opens the gate, and a Marauder's Journal says marauders took 'the dockmaster's acquisition' that opens a sealed ruin to their storeroom at Blind Robber's Bluff.

The final objective says Lurius rewards you, but the reward itself isn't in these extracts. The one spell tied to the quest script (Reanimate (Self)) is cast by Alberthor on himself, not given to you.
Whether each mercenary follows you into the barrow depends on globals set elsewhere (one per mercenary); how they get set isn't in these files.
Wyrmstooth Barrow's enemies run level 24-60 and Dimfrost's 24-79; the records don't say how hard the required route is.
Lurius waits at a spot on the dock that Holmar also uses, under a condition these files don't decode; when it doesn't hold, he waits inside the Red Wave instead.
The quest also tracks a marauder 'thief' placed in the barrow's refectory; whether he has anything to do with Goreduster isn't shown.

quests.name: The Naked Nord
journal: I have read a note mentioning a naked nord spotted in the wilderness seemingly unable to move. I should investigate this matter.
I ran across a nord that had been paralyzed by a witch, stripped of all he was worth, and left to die in the wilderness.

A naked nord I met in the wilderness has asked me to find the pants that were stolen from him by a witch that put him under a paralysis spell. He suspects the witch is part of a coven inhabiting an old castle on the island to the north-west of Wyrmstooth. I should also search for a way to free him of his paralysis.

I was able to track down the witch that stole Gjalrunn's pants, however it would seem she too had been accosted on the road and had the pants stolen from her by warlocks from Krakevisa. They are likely conducting a ritual to transpose the enchantment on the pants as we speak. I should head there as soon as possible to prevent that from happening.

I was unable to stop the ritual in time. The pants have been transposed, destroying them in the process. I should return to either Gjalrunn or Glendora and let them know what transpired. I should also seek a cure for Gjalrunn's condition.
I was able to retrieve the pants before the ritual could complete. From here I must decide to either give the pants to Glendora the witch or return them to Gjalrunn.
I have given the pants to the witch Glendora in return for a reward. I should still seek a cure for Gjalrunn's condition.
I have given the pants back to Gjalrunn for which he was most grateful. I should seek a cure for his condition next. Perhaps Glendora will be able to help with that.
I have lied to Gjalrunn about finding the pants. I should still seek a cure for his condition.
I have told Gjalrunn that I had given the pants to Glendora. He was noticeably upset by this. I should still seek a cure for his condition.

Gjalrunn has refused the antidote I obtained from Glendora. There is nothing more I can do for him, though I suspect he'll seek revenge in one form or another once the paralysis wears off on its own. Assuming he survives that long...
I have given both the pants and the antidote to Gjalrunn for which he was incredibly grateful. Perhaps we'll cross paths on the road again one day.

I have given Gjalrunn the antidote to cure his condition but lied about finding his pants. At least he was happy to be freed from the witch's magic. His pants are mine now and ought to fetch a nice sum of gold. Perhaps we'll cross paths on the road again one day.

I have given Gjalrunn the antidote to cure his condition but could not retrieve his pants in time before they were turned to ash by the warlock's ritual. At least he was happy to be freed from the witch's magic. Perhaps we'll cross paths on the road again one day.

After giving Gjarunn the antidote to cure his condition I told him that I had given the pants to the witch instead. He was noticeably incensed by this and vowed revenge in one form or another. I suspect he plans on taking the pants back from the witches himself. I doubt he will be able to.

Though I lied about finding Gjalrunn's pants I was able to obtain an antidote to cure his condition for which he was grateful. His pants are mine now and ought to fetch a nice sum of gold. Perhaps we'll cross paths on the road again one day.
I have lied to Gjalrunn about finding a cure for his paralysis. Dejected, he has asked me to put him out of his misery.
Gjalrunn has died. It is no longer possible to do anything about his situation.

unsure.why: The line's record order is not story order. The story runs Wyrmstooth, then Barrow of the Wyrm; most of the other quests need you on the island, which the records only show you reaching on the Red Wave during Barrow of the Wyrm.
How the four bounty jobs are handed out isn't in the records; the island has a 'Check the notice board for work' pointer, so they are probably taken from a notice board.
Whether the mercenaries' and Alberthor's favours are offered during the story or only after Barrow of the Wyrm isn't shown; their opening lines only check that the quest hasn't begun.
Stickler in the Mud only names the Deadlands; The Cause is the only quest in the files that takes you there, and whether you must finish it or only reach its Oblivion Gate isn't shown.
For Robbed Blind the records place Erikur in his house in Solitude and mark a coffin of his as holding the necklace, but the coffin's spot isn't in the files.
The records give enemy levels but not a level the island is made for: Wyrmstooth Barrow 24-60, Dimfrost 24-79, Bloodfrost Burrow's boss 55-125, Vulom level 51.
Lurius's reward for Barrow of the Wyrm, the price of Fort Valus and its upgrades, and most side-job rewards aren't named in the records.

No dialogue or event in the files starts Wyrmstooth; the courier's walk-to-you package needs the quest already running and your level at or above 20 (raised from 10 by a Requiem patch). Whether Theodyn gives the message below level 20 if you find him yourself isn't shown.

journal: That guard at Fort Tulis mentioned some disturbances deep in the depths of the fort that he thinks might be goblins. I should investigate.

I reported back to the guard, and told him I had killed all of the goblins under the fort. He thanked me but was concerned that they might return. The only way to stop them is if I track down and kill the clan's Shaman. I should search for him now.

I reported back to the guard, and told him I had not killed all of the goblins under the fort. He seemed disappointed, but said that they would return anyway. The only way to stop them is if I track down and kill the clan's Shaman. I should search for him now.

I reported back to the guard, and told him that I was unsure that I had killed all of the goblins under the fort. He told me they would likely return anyway. The only way to stop them is if I track down and kill the clan's Shaman. I should search for him now.
I have tracked down and killed the Goblins' Shaman. The guard at Fort Tulis has rewarded me, and the Bruska clan will be severely weakened now.
The guard at Fort Tulis is dead. The goblins will continue to ravage the valley and its inhabitants. At any rate, no-one will pay me for killing the Shaman now.

read.about: Separate side quests set in the city of Baan Malur and on the Morrowind mainland around it, at Fort Tulis, Cormaris and the craglands to the south. There are six quests to play, plus a ferry service between Morrowind's ports and Raven Rock on Solstheim and one empty placeholder.

The quests have no shared start; The Amulet of Old is the line's opening in the start records, but any of the others can be found first. Which route a new player should take to Baan Malur (the Raven Rock ferry or the Dwemer ruin Kalbthurz a book names as a way through) isn't set out in the records.
A Grand Venture is a bare placeholder; whether a script ever runs it isn't shown.
The New Temple's journal after you find Helvf Blackthorn is the author's placeholder notes with no objectives, so the later part may be unfinished.
The ferry checks something before offering Llethrin Fel, Pryai and Vivec, so those routes may need unlocking; how you book a crossing isn't in the records.
Bruska Shaman's Staff (a lightning staff) is linked to the Bruska Shaman only by its name; the other rewards are leveled lists or gold whose contents aren't in the records.
The sell-out endings of The Struggle for Justice have no ending marked in the journal; what happens to Kar-Jei and whether you are paid isn't in the records.

read.about: A short dungeon story on the Hjorkvild Isles, frozen islands north of Jehanna, where a necromancer holds the old Imperial fort Fort Icemoth with an army of undead, and a Nord barrow on the main island lies beyond it. Fort Icemoth is a level 24 to 50 dungeon and Winter Shroud Sanctum level 30 to 55; the line has two dungeon quests and two book quests.

journal: I had a strange vision in my mind. Also I know where to go now.
I've succesfully escaped from Coldharbour.
I just met a man named Arenar and I'm following him to his village. I am in a desert region, now.

So, I'm in Hammerfell, in an isolated region. Lady Syloria has told to me what I'll have to do. The mausoleum is located in the Oasis of Mora Sul at the East side of this region, but first I'll have to get two items. One is the key to the entrance in Mora Sul and it's located in Al Shedim, northern of Ben Erai. Another item is the Alliance of Ancestral Cheetahs amulet, located at very  north of this region. Let's go!

Finally I entered the Mausoleum of the Champion of Cyrodiil. Now I have to fire the Arrow of the Extrication. That tiny rug near the bow should be the position where I have to stay to fire the Arrow and the bluish disc at the opposite side is the thing where I have to hit it with the Arrow.
A door was opened along the right side of the Mausoleum. I think this is the great moment.
Finally I got the Gray Cowl of Nocturnal. Now I have to go back to Seviana by using the magic portal.
I've got the legendary Gray Cowl of Nocturnal.

I talked to Tenerio back in the Dark Brotherhood Sanctuary in the Alik'r Desert. He wants me to investigate the whereabouts of an initiate called Lucya. Apparently, she was the one sent to find me back in Skyrim back when the Sanctuary was just reinvested.

I found nothing but a dead vampire back in the Alik'r Desert. Nothing about Lucya, but it doesn't sound good if she was the one that murdered the nord. I should head back to tell Tenerio about what I found.
Tenerio told me of a forgotten warehouse that Lucya said she would like to investigate for a future use. She might have headed there, I should look around to see if I can find her there.
Lucya was found dead in the abandoned warehouse. It seems her soul was bound to a soul gem. I should head back to the Sanctuary and tell Tenerio about the tragedy.

Lucya was found dead in the abandoned warehouse. It seems her soul was bound to a soul gem. Tenerio told me she was after an artifact and that she had found a way to get to it, but she was murdered by vampires before she could try anything. But I know about the Soul Cairn, so I might be able to find her there.

read.about: A vision sends you to the Hall of the Initiation in Skyrim, and the Gray Cowl story then takes you through the Imperial City Prison, Sancre Tor and Coldharbour to the Alik'r Desert in Hammerfell, where you claim the Gray Cowl from a mausoleum. Reaching the desert also opens Betalille's Hammerfell quests in Ben Erai, Salas Kazas and the Wind Scour Temple; there are 40 quests in all, no level gate is set, and the desert's dungeons hold enemies from level 10 to 80.

unsure.why: No quest in the line carries a level gate; the level range is taken from the desert dungeons in the checked reads (Al Shedim 10 to 80, Khenzedum 15 to 60, Sadraaka level 40).

The quest is set to run from game start with no conditions; what moves it to the vision (a level, a time, a script) isn't in the records. Where the Key to Hall of the Initiation comes from, and which hold the Hall of the Initiation and Seviana's House stand in, aren't shown.
The Betalille quests are all in the Alik'r Desert, which The Call of Gray Cowl of Nocturnal takes you to; whether From Solstheim to Hammerfell is another way in isn't in the records.
The Call of Gray Cowl of Nocturnal probably takes you to Akavir near the end (a portal alias and Seviana's line about Hammerfell and Akavir); those stages have no text.

Time for the Farewells has no giver or start event in the records; it most likely follows the end of The Call of Gray Cowl of Nocturnal, and that Seviana and Luvien leave Skyrim for good is read from its title.
Helping the Enemy most likely comes after The Ash'abah (Honai's later packages assume it is done), but no condition says so.
The Dark Brotherhood in Hammerfell may need you to be in the Dark Brotherhood with the Dawnstar Sanctuary open; the conditions on the Unknown Initiate's line aren't in the records.
The order of Jukka's four museum quests and Tenerio's contracts is read from their journals; the conditions that unlock each one aren't in the records.

The six Dragonguard Archives books have no giver or start event; they probably start from a notice or note and probably come after A Lost Temple in Hammerfell, since the archive chest is in the Wind Scour Temple.
Where the Alik'r Desert Sanctuary, the Ash'abah Hideout, Vulstad, Arenar's Camp and most other desert places lie isn't in the places records.
Whether Ending the Dark Brotherhood in Hammerfell again ends Tenerio's contracts is read from its aliases; it swaps in a separate hostile Tenerio, and the script isn't read.

Many rewards are quest script properties not confirmed by a log line: the Left Eye of Coldharbour, the Unlock Container tome, Irlav's Penitence (what it does isn't in the item records), Respected by the Ash'abah (its effect isn't given), the Crimson Eviscerator from Leollus, and the gold amounts.
What triggers the failure of Memories of the Umbranox isn't in the records; that a missed journal is gone for good is a guess from the failure line.

quests.name: Lost in the Woods
journal: After "escaping" the cemetery house, I found myself somewhere I don't recognise. The house and trees are all the same, but the sky... Wherever this is, it isn't Falkreath.
After escaping the pit of bones and tar, I was greeted by an expansive underground city. It looks like someone's trying to burn the place down, and I think I might know who...
I found the writer of the notes, dead. The Temple behind him seems to be my goal, but first I'll have to close the barrier. His note mentions a building opposite the Temple...
I've defeated the Sentinel, only to find the Wraithmother dismounted it and disappeared. A red portal appears... It doesn't seem like I have any other option.
I'm back in Tamriel. Herrah has been consumed by the void, leaving everything with me. Lifesurge, her Axe, her life-stealing Scarlet Cloak... And Gravewind.

read.about: A story that starts at an abandoned homestead among graves and strange flowers in the Falkreath woods and leads into Gravewind, another realm reached through the house. It has three quests; the vampire lair that holds the key to the homestead has a boss leveled 55 to 125, and no other level gate is set.

getIn.where: the Cemetery Homestead in the woods of Falkreath; its key is on the vampire Vighar in Bloodlet Throne, Falkreath
getIn.how: Kill the vampire Vighar in Bloodlet Throne for the Cemetery Homestead Key, then unlock the abandoned homestead in the Falkreath woods and explore it.
needs: Cemetery Homestead Key, carried by Vighar in Bloodlet Throne (LoreRim puts this lock on the homestead's door)

order.what: Touching the light Richter left in Gravewind brings the realm down, and you have to escape before it falls.
order.needs: Reach Richter's light in Gravewind, through In the Pines and Lost in the Woods.

order.what: You unlock the abandoned homestead in the Falkreath woods and explore it; the door locks behind you and you have to find a way out.
order.where: Bloodlet Throne for the key; Cemetery Homestead, Falkreath
order.needs: The Cemetery Homestead Key from Vighar.

order.what: You step out of the homestead into a land that isn't Falkreath, follow the notes of a man named Richter through Gravewind's underground city, and find your way home.
order.needs: Finish In the Pines.

options: Touch Richter's light: Gravewind falls, the souls enthralled there are freed, and the house in the Falkreath woods is gone for good
Leave the light alone: Lost to Oblivion doesn't start and Gravewind stays as Lost in the Woods leaves it

gives: Lifesurge, a power: once a day, scarlet lightning completely restores your health
Herrah's Axe and her life-stealing Scarlet Cloak, named in the journal at the end of Lost in the Woods
Gravewind itself, left to you at the end of Lost in the Woods
Death Strider, at the end of Lost to Oblivion
closes: Herrah, the Wraithmother of Gravewind, is consumed by the void at the end of Lost in the Woods
Lost to Oblivion destroys Gravewind and the house in the Falkreath woods for good

unsure.why: The homestead's door stays hidden until another object is enabled, and what enables it isn't in the records. LoreRim's lock also edits Dark Ancestor, the quest whose alias holds Vighar; whether Vighar is in Bloodlet Throne without Dark Ancestor running isn't shown. Dengeir of Stuhn in Falkreath gives Dark Ancestor.
Richter's light is probably Richter's Flame in The Way Home, the last stretch of Lost in the Woods; whether Lost in the Woods must be finished before Lost to Oblivion isn't shown.

Herrah's Axe and the Scarlet Cloak are named only in the journal's last entry and nothing hands them over; the Infused Battleaxe is the mod's only battleaxe and may be her Axe, and no cloak from the mod is in the item records.
Death Strider is given through a script property named for a perk; its effect isn't in the spell or power records.
The power Expel Greater Spirit lets you expel the soul once trapped in the Gravewind Sentinel, but nothing ties it to Lost in the Woods.

quests.name: March of the Dead
journal: I've stumbled across a Dark Elf in combat for his life with strange, ashen beings at the Attius Farm outside of Raven Rock. He appears outnumbered, and he's requested I lend him a helping hand.

I've stumbled across Captain Modyn Veleth fighting strange beings called "ash spawn" at the Attius Farm outside of Raven Rock. Captain Veleth was outnumbered, so I engaged his attackers and lent him a helping hand.

Captain Veleth explained that the ash spawn have been attacking Raven Rock for some time now, and he's been trying to locate their source. His lack of manpower and reluctance to leave the town without a commander are keeping him from finding out more. As a result of our conversation, I've agreed to help him deal with this situation. I need to begin by searching the Attius Farm for clues that might lead me to the ash spawn's source.

While assisting Captain Veleth at the Attius Farm, I've discovered a strange note. I should give this note to Captain Veleth in order to learn more about the origins of the ash spawn threat to Raven Rock.

Captain Veleth was alarmed by the strange note I recovered from the ash spawn at the Attius Farm. The note mentions Fort Frostmoth, the ruins of an Imperial fort located southeast of Raven Rock. According to him, the fort's been abandoned ever since the eruption of Red Mountain. He's sent me to Fort Frostmoth to kill the author of the note, General Falx Carius, before the town falls prey to his threats.
I've slain General Falx Carius in the ruins of Fort Frostmoth and put an end to any further ash spawn attacking Raven Rock. I should return to Captain Modyn Veleth and inform him of my victory.
I've slain General Falx Carius in the ruins of Fort Frostmoth. I should examine his remains to determine what he was doing here.

According to the letter I found on General Carius' remains, he appeared to be responsible for sending what he calls his "men" to attack the town of Raven Rock. I should bring this information to the guards in Raven Rock and let them know the threat has been eliminated.

I've slain General Falx Carius in the ruins of Fort Frostmoth and put an end to any further ash spawn attacking Raven Rock. Captain Veleth was very pleased with my results, and awarded me a bounty in gold.

quests.name: Served Cold
journal: Captain Veleth told me that Adril Arano, Second Councilor of Raven Rock,  wanted to speak to me immediately. I should find him and discover the reason for his urgent message.

Adril Arano has requested my help with what he believes is an imminent threat on Councilor Morvayn's life. He believes members of the Ulen family are present on the island and seek revenge upon Morvayn for executing their ancestor. He's requested that I investigate the identity of any possible assassins, hoping to catch them unaware. For now, I've refused his request, but I should return to Adril when I'm ready to assist him.

Adril Arano has requested my help with what he believes is an imminent threat on Councilor Morvayn's life. He believes members of the Ulen family are present on the island and seek revenge upon Morvayn for executing their ancestor. He's requested that I investigate the identity of any possible assassins, hoping to catch them unaware. Adril suggests that I start by speaking to Geldis Sadri, the innkeeper at the Retching Netch Cornerclub. He's hoping that Geldis, who has quite the reputation as a gossip, might have some useful leads.

Geldis Sadri has pointed out that someone is leaving ash yam offerings in the Ulen Ancestral Tomb even though no Ulens live on Solstheim. He suggests that I stake the tomb out at night and discover the identity of the mystery visitor. Hopefully this person is either the assassin himself or can lead me to the assassin threatening Councilor Morvayn's life.

I discovered Tilisu Severin visiting the Ulen Ancestral Tomb at night. This seems suspicious, as she doesn't belong to the Ulen family by name. I should bring this piece of evidence to Adril Arano immediately.

I've informed Adril Arano that Tilisu Severin was the mystery visitor leaving offerings in the Ulen Ancestral Tomb. Since this is not enough evidence to accuse her of a crime, he's sending me to Severin Manor in order to uncover solid evidence that exposes Tilisu as an assassin.

I've recovered evidence from Severin Manor that exposes the true nature of the Severin family. The letters indicate that Vendil Severin is actually Vendil Ulen and that his supposed wife Tilisu and his daughter Mirri are members of House Hlaalu, one of the Great Houses that opposes Morvayn's House Redoran. All three of them are working in conjunction with unknown forces in a place called "Ashfallow Citadel," to assassinate Councilor Morvayn. I need to bring this urgent revelation to Adril Arano immediately.
Adril Arano has sent me to Ashfallow Citadel to destroy Vendil Ulen and whatever forces he's amassed there. I'm supposed to meet two Redoran Guard outside the ruins who will assist me in this regard.

Adril Arano has sent me to Ashfallow Citadel to destroy Vendil Ulen and whatever forces he's amassed there. I've found the two Redoran Guard I was supposed to meet there dead. I'll have to carry the fight into the ruins alone.

I've killed Vendil Ulen and stopped the threat against Councilor Morvayn. Vendil had hired assassins from Morrowind known as the Morag Tong to help him with his coup, but fortunately I was able to defeat them in the depths of Ashfallow Citadel. I should return to Adril Arano with the good news.
With Vendil Ulen dead and the Morag Tong eliminated, I've ended the threat to Councilor Morvayn and saved Raven Rock.

quests.name: The Final Descent
journal: I've stumbled across Crescius Caerellius inside of Raven Rock Mine. He's convinced that the mines of Raven Rock contain a secret important enough for him to risk his own life to discover. He appears to have more to tell, so I should listen to what he has to say if I want to learn more.

I've stumbled across Crescius Caerellius inside of Raven Rock Mine. He's convinced that the remains of his great-grandfather, Gratian Caerellius, are at the bottom of the mine and that the East Empire Company has falsely designated his ancestor's death as an accident. He's tasked me with exploring the mine on his behalf to locate the remains, and perhaps discovering what killed Gratian Caerellius.
I've located the skeletal remains of Gratian Caerellius. In his satchel, I've discovered an old journal. In order to return it to Crescius, I'll have to discover a way to escape Bloodskal Barrow.
After locating the remains of Gratian Caerellius, recovering his journal, and escaping Bloodskal Barrow, I should bring the evidence of my discovery to Crescius Caerellius.
I've located Gratian Caerellius' remains and uncovered the truth regarding his untimely death deep inside Bloodskal Barrow.

Served Cold's reward isn't decoded. A LoreRim patch named for Severin Manor having a price edits the quest and Councilor Morvayn's thank-you line; that points to Severin Manor being sold rather than given, but the records here don't show the price or the hand-over.

An Axe to Find is named as the lead-in to The Final Descent and Crescius is in both, but the records don't show it starting The Final Descent. What starts The Final Descent Priest isn't shown either, and whether the Seeker is Zahkriisos isn't settled.
Served Cold's need for March of the Dead is read from Adril Arano's line about everything you've already done for Raven Rock; the condition on Captain Veleth's opening line isn't in the files.
The conditions on the favor givers' opening lines aren't in the files, so whether March of the Dead or anything else must come first for the favors isn't known.
Gold amounts aren't in the records. Most favors list no reward at all; whether you pick up the Bloodskal Blade or are handed it isn't shown.
What happens to Tilisu and Mirri Severin in Served Cold isn't in the records.

quests.name: Retaking Thirsk
journal: I met a group of Nords from Thirsk Mead Hall, which has recently been overrun by rieklings. They're camped on the eastern shore of the island, waiting for an opportunity to attack and take back their home.
I've agreed to help the Nords from Thirsk Mead Hall take their home back from the rieklings who have infested it.
I helped the warriors of Thirsk Mead Hall retake their home from the infestation of rieklings.

I helped the warriors of Thirsk Mead Hall retake their home from the infestation of rieklings. Their leader, Bujold, has asked me to accompany her to Hrothmund's Barrow, where she hopes to receive the blessing of Thirsk's founder to continue her leadership.

I helped the warriors of Thirsk Mead Hall retake their home from the infestation of rieklings. Their leader, Bujold, asked me to accompany her to Hrothmund's Barrow, where she was denied the blessings of Thirsk's founder. She expressed a desire to lead the hall anyway, and when I opposed her fraud, she attacked me.

I helped the warriors of Thirsk Mead Hall retake their home from the infestation of rieklings. Their leader, Bujold, asked me to accompany her to Hrothmund's Barrow, where she was denied the blessings of Thirsk's founder. She expressed a desire to lead the hall anyway, and plans to begin a new tradition at Thirsk, focused on the present instead of the past.

I helped the warriors of Thirsk Mead Hall retake their home from the infestation of rieklings. Their leader, Bujold, asked me to accompany her to Hrothmund's Barrow, where she was denied the blessings of Thirsk's founder. She expressed a desire to lead the hall anyway, and when I opposed her fraud, she became enraged. I was forced to kill her to defend myself.
I met a group of Nords who had been exiled from their former home in Thirsk Mead Hall, but chose to help the rieklings keep them permanently evicted.

lines.begins: At Haknir's Shoal, a band of pirates uncovered an ancient treasure chest containing a single piece of stalhrim armor. How did they know to dig in this remote spot?

quests.name: Deathbrand
journal: At Haknir's Shoal, a band of pirates uncovered an ancient treasure chest containing a single piece of stalhrim armor. How did they know to dig in this remote spot?

A band of pirates followed an ancient treasure map to Haknir's Shoal, where they discovered a chest at the location marked on the map. By following the map, perhaps I can find the rest of the treasure they sought.

A band of pirates followed an ancient treasure map to Haknir's Shoal, where they found a chest containing a piece of the armor of Haknir Death-Brand, the legendary pirate king. By following their map, perhaps I can find the rest of the treasure they sought.

By following an ancient treasure map, I found the armor of Haknir Death-Brand, the legendary pirate king. In addition to his armor, one chest also contained the key to Gyldenhul Barrow. Could it be connected to Haknir's treasure?

By following an ancient treasure map, I found the armor of Haknir Death-Brand, the legendary pirate king. A key contained in one of the chests led me to Gyldenhul Barrow, where I found a room filled with Haknir's cursed gold. But touching it triggered the curse: the doors behind me have sealed.

By following an ancient treasure map, I found the armor of Haknir Death-Brand, the legendary pirate king. A key contained in one of the chests led me to Gyldenhul Barrow, where I found his tomb and one of his cursed swords. But when I touched the sword, his ghost appeared and attacked.

By following an ancient treasure map, I found the armor of Haknir Death-Brand, the legendary pirate king. A key contained in one of the chests led me to Gyldenhul Barrow, where I defeated Haknir's ghost and claimed his swords and gold as well.

quests.name: Unearthed
journal: Outside Kolbjorn Barrow, I met Ralis Sedarys, an explorer who came to Solstheim in search of relics within the barrow. But when he arrived, he found it buried by the ash. He had all but given up on excavating it, but if I can supply the funds, he offered to make me a partner in his expedition.

Ralis Sedarys came to Solstheim in search of the Relics of Ahzidal, powerful items said to have been sealed in Kolbjorn Barrow, but found it buried by ash. I agreed to fund his expedition to excavate the barrow. He set to work, saying he'd send a courier when he had progress to report.

journal: I met an Argonian called Haj-Xul at The Retching Netch in Raven Rock. He claims he is a member of the An-Xileel clan in Black Marsh and has hired me to assist him in capturing a criminal from House Telvanni who might have recently arrived in Solstheim.
I managed to find and defeat Zirath Ryon in the depths of the Ashbound Prison. However, the exit locked itself behind me, leaving me trapped unless I find a different way out.

I managed to defeat both Zirath Ryon and Durvith, the dragon priest who lured him to Solstheim in the first place, securing the power of Miasma for myself. For my efforts, Haj-Xul awarded me with his personal bow and named me a friend of the An-Xileel.

The mod adds a set of Miasma spells (Miasmic Spray, Stream, Bolt, Rune, Cloak, Cloud and Missile, each from a Tome of Miasma, plus Conjure Miasmic Thrall) and a dragon priest mask called Durvith that raises Miasma spell damage by 25%; these files don't say whether you are given any of them or find them.

The gold is named by the quest's script, not confirmed by the journal; how much isn't in these files. The bow and the An-Xileel friendship are in the closing journal entry.

quests.name: In My Time Of Need
journal: A group of men calling themselves the Alik'r are looking for a Redguard woman in Whiterun.

The barmaid at the Bannered Mare in Whiterun is apparently a fugitive noble from Hammerfell. She claims that she is on the run from assassins sent by rival houses in her homeland and needs someone to stop them before they find her.

The leader of the so-called "assassins" I've been asked to eliminate claims that Iman betrayed her people to the Dominion and they are here to bring her to justice. I've agreed to lead her into an ambush at the Whiterun stables.
I've helped Iman escape the clutches of the Alik'r sent after her. With their leader defeated, she believes the rest of them will scatter, affording her some much-needed safety for now.
After making arrangements with Kematu, I've delivered Iman to him. He assures me that she will be taken back to Hammerfell alive, though after that her fate is no longer in his hands.

quests.name: Missing In Action
journal: Fralia Gray-Mane in Whiterun is convinced that her missing son, Thorald, is still alive and being held captive. She's asked me to visit her at her home to speak privately about the matter.
Avulstein Gray-Mane believes his brother Thorald has been taken prisoner, and that the Battle-Borns of Whiterun have proof. I need to find it and bring it to Avulstein.
After being convinced to help by the Gray-Mane family, I've found evidence that Thorald Gray-Mane is still alive, and is being held in Northwatch Keep. Avulstein will want to see this right away.

After being convinced to help, and finding proof that he is still alive, I've offered to try and free Thorald Gray-Mane from Northwatch Keep, a Thalmor controlled fort on the northwestern coast, to prevent bloodshed on either side.

Now that I have found proof that his brother still lives, Avulstein Gray-Mane insists on assaulting Northwatch Keep, a Thalmor controlled fort on the northwestern coast, to rescue Thorald. I've agreed to meet him outside the Keep to assist in the fight.
Thorald Gray-Mane is indeed alive. Now I have to get him away from Northwatch Keep and make sure he stays safe.

Thorald Gray-Mane has been successfully retrieved from Northwatch Keep. Fearing for the safety of his family, he cannot return to Whiterun, and has asked me to deliver a message to his mother: "Suffer the winter's cold wind, for it bears aloft next summer's seeds."

Both amulets are quest script properties, but when each one is handed over isn't in these files. LoreRim's Necromancer's Amulet: improves spellcasting and lets very experienced enchanters craft black soul gems at midnight, but makes the weak-minded wither.
The Hjerim key is carried by Tova Shatter-Shield; the Unofficial Patch adds a replacement key. How you talk her into handing it over isn't in these files.

The second start is read from the journal: an opening objective to get the steward's help, and a Hjerim line that only shows when you haven't seen the murder scene. What sets it off isn't in these files.

The quest names Arivanya, placed at Windhelm Stables, as a second victim and holds spots for a third and a final one. Whether and when they die isn't in these files; the Unofficial Patch adds a step that keeps the second victim alive for a time.

journal: In my search for a cure for vampirism, I read a book entitled "Undeath Undone". As I was reading, a note addressed to Urag fell out from between the book's pages. Falion in Morthal is rumored to have studied vampires.  He might be able to cure the condition.

unsure.why: Rising at Dawn rewrites the opening, and several of Falion's lines now wait for an early hidden stage. The extracts don't show what sets that stage, or where 'Undeath Undone' sits.
The journal assumes you are a vampire and warns against being Blood-Starved. The vampirism check itself isn't readable in the extracts.

The journal says to meet Falion "at the Black Marsh at dawn", but the objective is just "Meet Falion at dawn". Rising at Dawn adds its own ritual circle, and Falion now speaks of a place "with unmistakably strong ties to Oblivion", so the site and its hold aren't in the extracts.
The script lists Vampire Lord Form (a Dawnguard spell), probably so it can be taken away. It isn't a reward. Both endings say the ritual fails.
Linking this to A Forlorn Hope comes from that mod's name and Falion's letter. The extracts don't show what sends the letter, or whether killing Falion blocks it.
Rising at Dawn adds a cure potion to this quest and has Falion talk about a potion that once cured vampirism, but the extracts don't show whether you can end up cured here.

lines.name: Forbidden Legend
lines.begins: In Reachwater Rock, I found a cryptic message that said the tomb here had been sealed, and should be forgotten forever. What is the story of this place?

quests.name: Forbidden Legend
journal: In Reachwater Rock, I found a cryptic message that said the tomb here had been sealed, and should be forgotten forever. What is the story of this place?
In Folgunthur, I found a cryptic message on the body of a powerful draugr, condemning him for his ancient crimes. What was his story? Why was he entombed with a broken amulet?
In Geirmund's Hall, I found a cryptic message on the body of a powerful draugr, condemning him for his ancient crimes. What was his story? Why was he entombed with a broken amulet?
In Saarthal, I found a cryptic message on the body of a powerful draugr, condemning him for his ancient crimes. What was his story? Why was he entombed with a broken amulet?

Long ago, the Archmage Gauldur was murdered, and his three sons were hunted down by King Harald's personal battlemage. The entire incident was covered up, their names struck from every record. But the legend survived. Perhaps someone still knows the truth of this ancient tale.

Long ago, the Archmage Gauldur was murdered, and his three sons were hunted down by King Harald's personal battlemage. The mage Daynas Valen spent his life searching for the truth of this tale, and came to Folgunthur with the key needed to unlock its secret.

Long ago, the Archmage Gauldur was murdered by his three sons, who stole his amulet of power and divided it among themselves. The brothers were hunted down in secret and sealed in tombs across Skyrim. To reclaim the amulet, I will need to seek out their final resting places.

Long ago, the Archmage Gauldur was murdered by his three sons, who stole his amulet of power and divided it among themselves. I defeated the brothers and reclaimed the fragments of the amulet. Perhaps Gauldur's tomb holds the secret to restoring it to its original form.

Long ago, the Archmage Gauldur was murdered by his three sons, who stole his amulet of power and divided it among themselves. I collected the fragments of the shattered amulet and brought them to Gauldur's tomb, where the ghosts of the three brothers ambushed me.

Long ago, the Archmage Gauldur was murdered by his three sons, who stole his amulet of power and divided it among themselves. I defeated the undead brothers, located the fragments of the shattered amulet, and forged it anew in Gauldur's tomb.

unsure.why: The quest runs silently before you meet Katria, and the records here don't show what first switches it on. It holds the book The Aetherium Wars and other lead-in books (two of them on adventurers' bodies out in the wilds), so reading one of those is the likely lead, but that isn't confirmed.

The four shard sites come from the quest's cells (Raldbthar Deep Market, the Dwarven Storeroom) and the book Uncovering the Aetherium Forge (Raldbthar, a storeroom outside Mzulft, atop Deep Folk Crossing); which shard alias sits where isn't spelled out in these files. The shard total is a global whose value isn't given; the journal says four.

The quest script points at the Aetherium Crown only; the three forge recipes all need the Aetherium Crest you carry. A patch also adds versions that use 2 Aetherium Dynamo Cores instead of the Crest. The Aetherial Staff's effect text isn't in these files.

The Aetherium Wars calls Arkngthamz 'the great research center in the southern Reach', and a follower's line says the same; the places index puts it in Falkreath hold with Dragon Bridge and Morthal as nearest towns, which doesn't fit. I went with the book.
Whether the Forge can still be used after the quest ends (to make the other artifacts with Dynamo Cores) isn't shown in these files.

quests.name: Black Book: Whispers of the Veil
journal: I have found and read the Black Book called "Whispers of the Veil" deep within Scourg Barrow, and found myself in Hermaeus Mora's realm of Apocrypha. The forbidden knowledge hidden here may be the secrets of the ritual the necromancer Antioch was seeking. I should press on to uncover it, or read the book again to escape.

I have uncovered the forbidden knowledge contained in the Black Book "Whispers of the Veil" from deep within Apocrypha. The arcane secrets of transcendence have flooded my memory and I now know the lost rituals necessary to make myself an undead Lich. I have commited the ritual and it's components to parchment, and with the proper materials and preparation, I will have the means to become immortal.

quests.name: The Path of Transcendence
journal: From the forbidden secrets I learned in Apocrypha, I have inscribed a dark ritual to parchment that when completed, will allow me to transform into an undead Lich. I should begin to seek out the components necessary for the ritual.
I have purchased the necessary items and prepared a secure location at which to conduct the ritual.
I have successfully crafted my Phylactery, a vessel required to contain my own soul during, and after, the ritual.
I have managed to successully brew the Elixir of Defilation, a potent physical and spiritual poison which is necessry to complete my transformation during the ritual.

I now have all the necessary components to begin the Ritual of Transcendence. I should go to the Ritual Site and begin. I must make sure that I am ready, for once the transformation is complete it cannot be reversed. As an undead Lich, my power will increase tenfold, but I will be feared and hated by the people of Skyrim...
I am ready to begin the Ritual of Transcendence. If any component of the Ritual is missing or is not exact, it will surely fail and I will be killed...

I have completed the Ritual of Transcendence and become a powerful undead Lich. While in my true form I will be hated and feared, however I am able to use powerful magic from the school of Illusion to disguise myself as my previous mortal appearance.

The reward names come from script properties; their effect text isn't in these files. The mod also has 'Assume Lich Form' and 'Revert Form' lesser powers, but these files don't tie them to this quest.

The journal says you 'purchased the necessary items and prepared a secure location'; the two site options come from the quest's Sewer and Tower aliases and the upgrade books 'Solitude Sewers - Ritual Chamber' and 'Ravenscorn Spire - Laboratory'. The seller is probably The Broker, a merchant from this mod found at The Broker's Shack who belongs to its upgrades-merchant group; prices and where the shack is aren't in these files.

quests.name: In their Footsteps
journal: I have heard a rumor that a Vigil of Stendarr caravan has been attacked on the road somewhere in the Reach. I should investigate.

I have discovered the scene of the destroyed Vigil of Stendarr caravan in the Reach. While a bloody ambush has occurred here, it does not look as though the Forsworn were involved. I should investigate the devastation and see what I can find...

From a note I found on the body of a Necromancer, I have learned that the Vigil of Stendarr seemed to be transporting some sort of tome or artifact. Considering the size of the caravan's escort, it is clear it must be very important. It appears that the attackers have taken it to Ravenscorn Spire.

I have arrived at Ravenscorn Spire, the lair of the dark wizards that attacked the Vigil of Stendarr's caravan. I believe that the artifact they have stolen must be hidden inside. I should begin my search, and proceed with caution.

I have read the journal of the Necromancer's leader, Antioch. It appears that the dark artifact that was stolen from the Vigil of Stendarr was a powerful necromantic tome which has set him on the path of  completing some sort of dark ritual. I should search the Tower basement for more clues.

I have read another entry of Antioch's journal. It appears that he is seeking the secrets for a ritual that will allow him to transform into an undead Lich, and has already departed for the Dragontail Mountains in search of something. He has sent his followers across Skyrim to obtain more artifacts. I should stop them and see if they hold more clues to where their leader has gone.

I have searched Ravenscorn Spire, the lair of the Necromancers who assaulted the Vigil of Stendarr's caravan.  While I did not find the book that was stolen, I have learned that their leader, Antioch, is seeking to use it to become an immortal undead Lich. He has already departed for the Dragontail Mountains in search of something, but has sent his followers across Skyrim to obtain more artifacts. I should seek out and stop his minions before they cause more damage, and see if they have more clues that will lead me to him.

quests.name: Exhuming Power
journal: The Necromancer's leader, Antioch, is seeking to use a Tome stolen from the Vigil of Stendarr to become an undead Lich. He has already departed for the Dragontail Mountains in search of something, but has sent one of his followers to Winterhold to locate and dig up the body of a former Archmage from the College of Winterhold. I should find them and prevent them from taking what they are seeking.
I have found the gravesite of former Archmage Vyngald, which is being desecrated by Antioch's Necromancer followers. I must stop them.

I have discovered and defeated a group of Antioch's Necromancer followers who were desecrating Archmage Vyngald's burial ground, before they were able to obtain the raiment they were seeking. I can re-cover Archmage Vyngald's grave site and allow him to rest in peace, or take the Shroud of Vyngald from the coffin myself...
I have re-covered Archmage Vyngald's grave, allowing him to rest in peace.
I have taken the Shroud of Vyngald from the former archmage's desecrated grave. His enraged spirit appeared and attacked me, but I have defeated it.

quests.name: Arkay the Enemy
journal: The Necromancer's leader, Antioch, is seeking to use a Tome stolen from the Vigil of Stendarr to become an undead Lich. He has already departed for the Dragontail Mountains in search of something, but has sent some of his followers to  destroy a Temple of Arkay in Falkreath hold and take the Heart of one of its Priests. I should hurry there and stop them.
I have located the Temple of Arkay, but the Necromancers may already be here. I should proceed with caution.

The Necromancers had arrived at the Temple before me and slaughtered many of the Priests of Arkay before I finally defeated them. There is however one survivor from whom they were going to take extract the Heart for their ritual. I should free him, or I can take his Heart for myself...
I have freed the surviving Priest of Arkay.
I have slaughtered the surviving Priest of Arkay. I should now extract his Heart myself.

After reaching the Temple of Arkay and defeating the Necromancers I found there, I killed the surviving Priest of Arkay, and cut out his heart for the Necromancer's ritual. For some reason, I suspect this will come in handy.
After reaching the Temple of Arkay and defeating the Necromancers I found there, I released the surviving Priest of Arkay and let him escape.

quests.name: Infernal Alchemy
journal: The Necromancer's leader, Antioch, is seeking to use a Tome stolen from the Vigil of Stendarr to become an undead Lich. He has already departed for the Dragontail Mountains in search of something, but has sent some of his followers to conduct some sort of Alchemical Ritual on a plateau overlooking the Reach. I should investigate this.
I have arrived at the Ritual Site, where several of Antioch's followers seem to be preparing some sort of Cauldron and Reagents. I should dispose of them.

I have defeated the Necromancers at the Ritual Site. Their strange concoction however seems to be prepared and ready for reagents. I can destroy it to ensure the mixture is never completed, or I can try to finish the Elixirs they were trying to create myself...
I have destroyed the Cauldron and its contents. The Necromancer's foul concoction can never be completed now.

I attempted to complete one of the concoctions that the Necromancers were trying to complete at a strange Cauldron I found. I was not able to succeed however. The Cauldron has lost its potency and now the mixture can never be completed...

I attempted to complete one of the concoctions that the Necromancers were trying to create at a strange Cauldron I found. I have succeeded, and claimed the Elixir, 'Namira's Corrosion'. I should hold onto this until I can discover its use...

quests.name: Scourg Barrow
journal: I have defeated all of Antioch's followers throughout Skyrim as they attempted to obtain various artifacts and components for him. I should search their bodies and see if they hold any clues as to their leader's whereabouts.

From a note I found on the body of a Necromancer, I have learned that their leader, Antioch, has traveled deep into the Dragontail Mountains in search of an ancient crypt known as 'Scourg Barrow'. He believes that he is closer than ever to the forbidden secrets he is searching for. I should hurry to the Dragontail Mountains myself, and put a stop to him before he finds what he is looking for.

I have arrived at a frigid cliffisde trail, deep in the peaks of the Dragontail Mountains. An ancient crypt known as 'Scourg Barrow' is allegedly hidden here, where the Necromancer Antioch is attempting to unearth dark and forbidden knowledge. I should seek it out and put a stop to him.

I have entered the ancient crypt known as Scourg Barrow. The Necromancer Antioch is undoubtedly in the depths of these forgotten catacombs, seeking its forbidden secrets. I should find him and put a stop to his search personally.

Antioch is defeated, and his artifacts and knowledge now lie in my possession, thus ending the threat to Skyrim. The secrets that he was searching for in these catacombs may still lie within, however...

quests.name: A Plea From Granite Hill
journal: A courier handed me a note from someone in Granite Hill. I should read it.

Someone named John sent me a letter and asked me to meet him in Granite Hill. The letter mentioned that a shop owner named Privous along with John discovered a crawl space under Privious' shop, Oddities and Curiosities which led to a ruin filled with draugr.
John mentioned that the crawl space opened up into an old ruin where he saw draugr and heard strange noises. He gave me a key to the crawl space so I can clear out the draugr for him.

I went into the crawl space which led into the ruins John mentioned. It was filled with draugr which was expected but at the bottom of the of the tomb, I found and killed a dragon. I should go tell John about this and collect my reward.

I told John about the ruins found under the shop in Granite Hill. He was surprised to hear about the dragon and relieved I took care of the threat. He said he and the people of Granite Hill were thankful. I was given the keys to a home in Granite Hill as a reward.

quests.name: Kagrenac's Tools
journal: I've received an anonymous note from the courier. I should read it and see what it's regarding.
An individual name Mathis Valen urgently request to meet me at the Silver-Blood Inn in the city of Markarth. I should go and find out why.
I've met Mathis Valen, who knows the locations of the Lost Tools of Kagrenac. He has told me where to find them and how to restore them to their former power.
I've obtained the cursed key from Vonos Dreloth and now have access to Sunder's hiding place. I should now locate and retrieve Sunder.

I have convinced Yassour Tansumiran to tell me the whereabouts of Wraithguard; he has divulged his information regarding Wraithguard. It was stolen from him by a thief, and last he saw, it was being taken to the Dwemer ruins of Nchardak. Directly East, away from Raven Rock. I should now head towards Nchardak to reclaim Wraithguard.

I've acquired both Sunder and Wraithguard. However, they feel severely weakened over the last few centuries after the Heart of Lorkhan was banish by the Nerevarine. The Bal am as Aedra stones should be capable of restoring the tools on the pedestal in Blackreach. I should now travel to these Ayleid ruins near the Cyrodilic border.

I've obtained all three Bal am as Aedra stones, and the gems emit radiating energy from within me. Coursing through my very veins as if I were a god! I should now return to Mathis Valen at the Silver-Blood Inn in Markarth.
Mathis Valen has instructed me to meet him in Blackreach, where the pedestal location is. I should now travel to Blackreach and finally witness the restoration of Kagrenac's Tools.
A mysterious portal resides within this ruin. Mathis did not mention such a portal, but maybe it should be where he went. I should head into the portal and see where it takes me.

The portal has sent me to what appears to be an unfamiliar region not belonging to Skyrim. I need to find the entrance to the ruins to join Mathis's quest to restore the tools. Still, I should tread carefully, not fully understanding what has happened.

I have entered what seems to be a colossal Dwarven lift with no way down but to jump below... I need to continue ahead and meet with Mathis at the pedestal. Although exploring this place could reveal other hidden treasures too.
Ultimately it is unveiled that Mathis Valen is the leader of the remnants of the Sixth House and is scheming to use Kagrenac's Tools to reclaim Morrowind.

With Mathis Valen defeated along with both his bodyguards, a disaster is averted, however, the Sixth House of Dagoth Ur whereabouts and strength remains an elusive mystery. I should now head on over to the pedestal where I can restore Kagrenac's Tools to their former glory.
The Tools of Kagrenac have lastly restored to their former glory! I now am left with the fate of these tools to bring righteousness or misfortune to the mortal plane.

unsure.why: The quest starts when an item enters your inventory (two start nodes). The quest also tracks Keening, so getting Keening may be the trigger, but the conditions aren't in these files.
The plugin has both weakened and full-power Sunder, Wraithguard and Keening, and the quest script touches Keening and the weakened Sunder; exactly which items you end up holding isn't spelled out.

The journal sends you to Ayleid ruins near the Cyrodiil border for three stones. The records tie Oio-Lalor and Aba-Malatar to this quest; the mod's third ruin, Atalatar (Falkreath), isn't tied to it, so where each stone lies isn't certain.
Mathis Valen is flagged essential in the records, yet the quest has you defeat him; a script likely clears that, but it isn't shown here.
Mathis is placed in the Silver-Blood Inn and only has stay-near-his-spot packages, so he should be there at all hours.

The quest holds the Keening dagger as a script property and starts when an item enters your inventory, so picking up Keening may be what sets it off or a later step may need it; the records don't say.
The quest has a dragon and a spot for it to appear; when and where it shows up isn't in these files.

quests.name: Deluge of Deceit
journal: The Black-Briars sent out a notice for diving work to collect ingredients at the bottom of Lake Honrich. I should speak to Frissa Black-Briar at Elgrim's Elixirs if I want to accept the job.

I found a plant that seems to sing to me, at the bottom of Lake Honrich. I can see a cave behind it, but some kind of magic is stopping me from uprooting it. Maybe an alchemist within the city would know more?

I spoke with Frissa Black-Briar, who is paying for any samples and artifacts that I may find in the cave at the bottom of Lake Honrich. A hired team has already been dispatched there. They should be north of the Riften docks, by Merryfair Farm.
I found the Black-Briar's hired team by Lake Honrich. The Elven woman there said to speak to Ingun's assistant, the Argonian, once I'm ready to leave.
I spoke to the leader of the Black-Briar's diving team, and we are ready to proceed. I need to swim to the lowest point of Lake Honrich, and investigate the cave.
After uprooting a plant in the cave under Lake Honrich, the cavern collapsed, trapping me inside ruins deeper underground. I need to find another way to escape.

In the Ayleid ruins, I found a massive hall with many connecting doors. Tilael said that she needs time to rest, and will wait here for me. The bridge above is out of reach, but there may be a path I can take here, somewhere. There's also another pedestal, where I can place another Varla stone.
I found a Topaz Varla stone that seems to match the gem type on the pedestal in the main hall. I should return there, and explore my options after placing it.

I placed the Varla stone in the main hall, causing the room to flood. The water level is high enough for me to swim up to the bridge in the center. I can explore more of the area to look for a way out now.
I've escaped the Ayleid ruins. I should rest.

I fell into a trance while attempting to progress through the ruins, and met a ghostly woman who had ill intentions. I should find the other team members quickly and escape before they are affected by the magic here.

I placed a third Varla Stone on the pedestals in the Atasel Hall, causing the water to rise higher and give access to another platform. I should continue looking for the team members and a way to escape.
I placed all four Varla stones on the pedestals in the Atasel Hall, causing a portal to appear on the bridge. Could this be the way to get out of these ruins?

After going through the portal, I found the resting place of the Ayleid haunting this place, and put them to rest. With their magic no longer keeping the structure together, the halls are flooding. I need to find a way out!
I escaped the Ayleid ruins. I should return to Elgrim's Elixirs to talk to Frissa Black-Briar.
I spoke with Frissa Black-Briar about the Ayleid ruins, and she compensated me for the danger I was put in while trapped in the ruins.

I have reached Ever-Bog, I shoud search for the ingredients needed.
All the ingredients needed have been found, there should be a cooking station I can use to them at.
I should venture deeper into Ever-Bog to find this so called heart.

The poison seemed to have worked when applied to the heart, I should return and speak with the Villinian.
After speaking with Gwilym he has informed me that he will return to the heart, he should be there in a day if I want to witness him go about his duties.
After returning to Vinillian, he paid me and told me to be on my way.

unsure.why: The opening runs on a change-location event with no conditions shown; how the note is delivered (courier or straight into your pack) isn't in these files.
The prison is in the mod's own cells, which have no name in these files; you're moved in and out by the quest (portal aliases), so where it sits in Skyrim isn't shown.

Who you report Nirenoore to isn't named; Kelkemmeriil, a Thalmor, has lines up to that point and is the likely one. Which choice leads to the hammer-and-circlet or nothing-to-give endings is read from the log text only.

The reward aliases (sword, shield, wings and so on) are filled from objects the extract doesn't resolve, so the exact pieces aren't known. They may be the Welkynar Hussar set from the companion armor mod. The Footwraps and Ragged Trousers in the script are the prisoner clothes you're given in the cell, not a reward.
Nirenoore is placed in a holding cell; her package keeps her in the Bannered Mare once the quest is past the note.
The places index puts Embershard Mine in Falkreath hold, next to Riverwood.

Drinking with Nirenoore and A Welkynar Legend belong to the same mod and are offered by Nirenoore, who only waits at the Bannered Mare once this quest is under way, but no record says this quest unlocks them.
Nirenoore leads you to her hiding place; the records only say it is near Embershard Mine ('There is a bandit camp nearby. Embershard Mine I think.').

read.about: A side story about Nirenoore, a Welkynar knight hiding from the Thalmor, who asks for your help after a note calls you to the Bannered Mare in Whiterun; it takes you to Thalmor Headquarters in Solitude, a Thalmor prison and Embershard Mine. It is one main quest plus three smaller ones Nirenoore offers once she waits at the Bannered Mare.

options: Report Nirenoore to the Thalmor: you get some gold and the quest fails.
Agree to help her: the theft at Thalmor Headquarters and the rest of the quest.
Get her belongings back and accept her reward, or turn the reward down and end with nothing.
End it with her belongings still lost: she gives you her hammer and circlet, or has nothing to give.
Tell Nirenoore you're not interested: the quest fails.
Agree to look into it: buy the book from Urag, read it and show it to her.

gives: Nirenoore's recovered belongings (the quest holds a sword, shield, wings, pauldrons, helmet, bracers, boots, cape, body armor and a book), if you accept her reward in The Welkynar Knight
Welkynar Hussar Hammer and Welkynar Hussar Circlet, on one of the endings where her belongings stay lost
The artifacts Nirenoore sends you after in her radiant job
closes: Reporting Nirenoore to the Thalmor ends The Welkynar Knight
Failing to rescue Nirenoore before the Thalmor take her across the border ends The Welkynar Knight

unsure.why: No level gate shows in the records (no start conditions), so the level the line is made for isn't given.

The three smaller quests start on a location-change event plus Nirenoore's line; whether The Welkynar Knight must be finished first isn't in the files. Nirenoore stays at the Bannered Mare once the main quest is past its note, but a mod setting can send her to a home the files don't name. The artifact job's name is filled in with the artifact's name when it starts, and which artifacts and dungeons it picks isn't recorded.
The belongings aliases are filled from objects the extract doesn't resolve, so the exact pieces aren't known. Which ending gives the hammer and circlet is read from the log text only.
How the note is delivered (courier or straight into your pack) isn't in the files.

Falk Firebeard is a quest alias and the Blue Palace is the one cell the quest uses, but no dialogue of his is recorded.

In the dossier, the Inner Sanctum passage sits under the Helm, and the Stendarr's Beacon passage sits just before the Helm, after the Cuirass and Gauntlets headings.

quests.name: The Thalmor's Shadow
journal: I heard rumors about a statue of Talos hidden somewhere in the Falkreath area. Perhaps I could find some allies that could help me.

Unfortunately, looks like the Thalmor found the statue before I could. However, there is one member still alive. He refuses to give me his real name, going by an alias; Taliesin. He's injured pretty badly, but seems harmless for the most part. Perhaps if I get him talking again, he may be of some use.

"Taliesin" seems cooperative at the moment. I can either heal him as promised, or leave him to bleed to death. Despite his bemoaning and caterwauling, the wound isn't that serious. A small potion should help.

I helped an injured member of the Thalmor at the statue of Talos. He still refuses to tell me his real name, but has offered to travel with me as thanks. Seems he's done with the Thalmor, however his loyalty and true intentions have yet to surface. I better keep an eye on him should I let him follow.

quests.name: Collecting the Edda - Windhelm
journal: Player has read the book

Higil in Windhelm has asked me to collect eddas from citizens of Windhelm. I got a list with all people I should speak to. I should start by speaking to Thane Alarik. He lives in the Higher Valunstrad. West of the palace. Look for him at court, if he is not at home.
Next on the list is Jorn Scarred-Scald. He lives in the Iron Quarter. East of the Palace. Close to the Pit. He tends to play in Iron Hall during the evenings.
Next on the list is Hellte. She works and lives in Iron Hall. The serving maid. She usually wears a bronze headband. Be careful.
Next on the list is Audmund.  Never thought him to be a writer, but you'll most like find him in his shop. The one between the Gray Quarter and the Iron Quarter. Close to the Pit.
Next on the list is Tormund. Tormund Tall-Tale. Heard he moved in to the old bookshop.The one right of Candlehearth Hall. Not sure if he actually owns the shop himself, now that I think about it.
Next on the list is Sulvar.  If he's still alive alive you'll find him in the Old Wheelhouse, outside the city. Think there's a gate from the market you can use. Been a while since I last saw him.

Next on the list is Frida Lives in the Valunstrad, just downstair from our clan's hall.  Big girl. Wears a bear pelt. Hard to miss. Very traditional. Might be at Wilhelm's place in the market, or at the Five Hundred's Wall, if not at home.
Next on the list is Hjarrandi. Old man. Lives up in the Hall of Relics. Up high, west of the palace. Know him for years, but still don't know much about him. Bit of a mystery, that one.
I should return to Higil with all the verses
Deliver to Higil.

journal: Player gets note

The Jarl is looking for someone to deal with some troublesome giants, who has their camp in the Tundra outside Whiterun. They way I see it, there's three ways I could deal with them. Honorable, but dangerous battle. Poison their food. Dishonorable, but effective. Or perhaps diplomacy. I could ask around town to see if there's anyone who knows more. There's people both inside and outside wall, someone will probably know something.
Urik claims to know how to deal with the Giants peacefully. I could read his note if, if diplomacy is my goal.

quests.name: On Hogithum
journal: I have discovered the fragment of a poem. That seems interesting. Perhaps I should explore at the Bard's College to see what this is all about.
I found a report at the Bard's college. It mentions a song, and suggests some places where I might find more about it. Giraud Gemane would probably be happy if I found them all.
I think I found all pieces of the lost poem, but it seems that the last verse is still missing. Perhaps Giraud Gemane can help.

Giraud was ecstatic and rewarded me with a copy of the collated fragments, including the last verse. According to Adonato's letter, it might be risky to read the complete version, but I can't resist the temptation. Surely nothing terrible can come out of it.
A tale of old has now been told, A bard's reward is due; A queen once brewed a lethal food, And you can brew it too.

quests.name: In the Shadows
journal: With the death of King Torygg, it seems not even the Jarls are safe in Skyrim, and security comes at a premium. Given the need for capable warriors, I should speak with the steward and see if he has any work for me.
In Whiterun, I spoke to the Jarl's steward and asked him if he had any work. He handed me a note with details on a job.

In Whiterun, I spoke to the Jarl's steward and asked him if he had any work. He handed me a note with details on a job. Reading the note, it seems there may be a potential assassination plot against the Jarl. The steward wants me to visit the local alchemist and check if anyone has purchased any poisons.

It seems there may be a potential assassination plot against the Jarl. At the steward's direction, I visited a local alchemist and took a copy of her ledger. I should read it to see if anyone has recently purchased any poisons.

It seems there may be a potential assassination plot against the Jarl. At the steward's direction, I visited a local alchemist and took a copy of her ledger. I read it and found two people had purchased poisons. A priest at the Hall of the Dead, and a stable boy.

It seems there may be a potential assassination plot against the Jarl. At the steward's direction, I visited a local alchemist and took a copy of her ledger. I read it and found two people had purchased poisons. A priest at the Hall of the Dead, and a stable boy. At the Whiterun Stables I found a dead body and clues that point to the Silent Moons Camp. I should investigate the area and see what I can find.

At the Silent Moons Camp, I discovered a journal from an assassin who intends on killing the Jarl of Whiterun. He intends to take the shot from somewhere unoccupied, using the Bow of Shadows to conceal himself. It's likely he will only appear when the Jarl is not tending to any other business. I should find him and take him out before he can carry through with the plot.
At the Silent Moons Camp, I discovered a journal from an assassin who intends on killing the Jarl of Whiterun. After following his trail, I found him in Dragonsreach and eliminated him.
